lessons.title: How Do You Read a Map?
lessons.blurb_en: Turn a 3D model of an island town until you look straight down and the buildings turn into symbols. Then measure distances with the scale and find your way with the north arrow and the legend.
lessons.blurb_zh: 把一座小島小鎮的 3D 模型轉到正上方，看房子變成地圖符號。再用比例尺量距離，用北方箭頭和圖例找路。
lessons.big_idea_en: Every map is a view from above, made smaller and drawn with symbols. To read any map, first find three things: the scale, which way is north, and the legend.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 每一張地圖都是從上往下看、縮小、再用符號畫出來的。看任何一張地圖，先找三件事：比例尺、哪邊是北、圖例。

lab.title_en: From a Model to a Map
lab.how_en: Press “Look straight down,” or pull the slider, and watch the camera turn until it looks straight down on the town. The buildings, trees, and lighthouse fade away and map symbols take their place. Choose a smaller area to see the same place at a larger scale, drag left or right to turn the island and watch the north arrow, and click a symbol in the legend to find it. The island and town are imaginary.
lab.how_zh: 按「轉到正上方」或拉動滑桿，看鏡頭慢慢轉到小鎮的正上方。房子、樹和燈塔淡出，換成地圖符號。選小一點的範圍，就是用大一點的比例尺看同一個地方；左右拖曳轉動小島，看北方箭頭怎麼跟著轉；點圖例裡的符號，找找它在哪裡。這座島和小鎮都是虛構的。

legend.en: North arrow: which way is north
Scale bar: how long a distance on the map is on the ground
legend.zh: 圖形比例尺：地圖上的長度在地面上是多遠

legend.en: Map symbols, explained in the legend
legend.zh: 地圖符號，意思寫在圖例裡

lab.scale_en: The island is 10 km across. Heights in the model are drawn 1.5 times taller than they really are. The ratio scales assume the view is printed 20 cm wide.
lab.scale_zh: 這座島寬 10 公里，模型裡的高度畫成實際的 1.5 倍。比例尺的數字，是假設這個畫面印成 20 公分寬。
lab.credit_html: The island, the town, and every name on this page are imaginary. The map symbols were drawn for this page and are not any agency's official symbols. · 這座島、小鎮和頁面上所有的地名都是虛構的。地圖符號是本頁自己畫的，不是任何機關的官方圖例。

paras: Imagine you are standing on a hill above a small town. You can see roofs, roads, a river, and fields. Now imagine rising higher and higher until you are looking straight down. The town looks flat, and everything in it looks small. A map is a drawing of that view from above, made smaller so that it fits on a sheet of paper or a screen.

A map cannot show things as they really look, so it uses symbols. A blue line can mean a river, a small flag can mean a school, and green with little dots can mean a forest. Different maps use different symbols, so every good map has a legend, also called a key. The legend is a small table that tells you what each symbol means. When you meet a map you have never seen, the legend is the first place to look.

The second thing to find is direction. On most maps, north is at the top, south is at the bottom, east is on the right, and west is on the left. Between them are northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest. But not every map is drawn that way, so look for a north arrow. If the arrow points somewhere else, turn the map in your mind until the arrow points up.

The third thing is the scale. The scale tells you how much smaller the map is than the real ground. A scale of 1:25,000 means that 1 centimeter on the map stands for 25,000 centimeters on the ground, which is 250 meters. Many maps also have a scale bar, a short line marked with a distance such as 500 meters. If the map is enlarged or shrunk, the bar changes with it and stays correct, but the number 1:25,000 does not. You can lay a ruler or the edge of a piece of paper along the bar to measure any distance on the map.

The same place can be drawn at different scales. A map of a whole country fits on one page only if it is made much smaller, so it shows less detail. A map of one neighborhood can show every building. Mapmakers call the second kind a large-scale map, because the fraction 1/5,000 is larger than 1/500,000. This sounds backward to many people, so it is worth remembering.

With these three things, you can answer real questions. How far is it from the school to the harbor? Use the scale. Which way should you walk from the bridge to reach the lighthouse? Use the north arrow. Is the green patch beside the road a forest or a rice field? Use the legend. Reading a map is not memorizing it. It is asking the map good questions.
paras_zh: 想像你站在一座小鎮旁邊的山丘上，看得到屋頂、道路、一條河和田地。現在想像你越升越高，直到從正上方往下看。小鎮看起來是平的，每樣東西都變得很小。地圖就是把這個從上往下看的樣子畫下來，再縮小到一張紙或一個螢幕放得下。
地圖沒辦法把東西照它真正的樣子畫出來，所以用符號。藍色的線可以代表河，小旗子可以代表學校，綠色加上小點點可以代表森林。不同的地圖用不同的符號，所以好的地圖都有圖例。圖例是一張小表，告訴你每個符號代表什麼。遇到一張沒看過的地圖，第一個要看的就是圖例。
第二件要找的是方位。大多數的地圖上方是北、下方是南、右邊是東、左邊是西；它們之間還有東北、東南、西南、西北。但不是每一張地圖都這樣畫，所以要找北方箭頭（學術名詞叫「指北標」）。如果箭頭指向別的方向，就在心裡把地圖轉一轉，讓箭頭朝上。
第三件是比例尺。比例尺告訴你地圖比真正的地面縮小了多少。比例尺 1:25,000 的意思是：地圖上的 1 公分，代表地面上的 25,000 公分，也就是 250 公尺。很多地圖還有圖形比例尺，是一小段標著距離（例如 500 公尺）的線。地圖被放大或縮小時，這段線會跟著一起變，所以仍然是對的；1:25,000 這個數字就不對了。把尺或一張紙的邊對著它，就能量地圖上任何一段距離。
同一個地方可以用不同的比例尺來畫。整個國家的地圖要縮得很小才放得進一頁，所以畫得比較粗略；一個街區的地圖可以把每一棟房子都畫出來。製圖的人把後面那一種叫做「大比例尺」地圖，因為 1/5,000 這個分數比 1/500,000 大。很多人覺得這說法剛好反過來，所以值得記住。
有了這三件事，就能回答真正的問題。從學校到港口有多遠？用比例尺。從橋要往哪個方向走才會到燈塔？用北方箭頭。公路旁邊那一片綠色是森林還是稻田？用圖例。讀地圖不是把地圖背起來，而是向地圖問好問題。
questions: Why does every good map need a legend?
A map has the scale 1:50,000. Two towns are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they on the ground?
Which shows more detail: a map at 1:5,000 or a map at 1:500,000? Which one is called the large-scale map?
answers: Different maps use different symbols, so the legend tells you what each symbol means on this particular map.
The 1:5,000 map shows more detail, because it covers a smaller area. It is the large-scale map, because 1/5,000 is a larger fraction than 1/500,000.

vocab.ex: The scale of this map is 1 to 25,000.
vocab.exzh: 這張地圖的比例尺是 1 比 25,000。

vocab.ex: Check the legend to see what the blue line means.
vocab.exzh: 看看圖例，就知道藍色的線代表什麼。

vocab.ex: A small flag is the symbol for a school on this map.
vocab.exzh: 在這張地圖上，小旗子是學校的符號。

vocab.ex: Which direction is the harbor from here?
vocab.exzh: 港口在這裡的哪個方向？

vocab.ex: The summit is to the northeast of the school.
vocab.exzh: 山頂在學校的東北方。

vocab.ex: Use the scale bar to measure the distance.
vocab.exzh: 用圖形比例尺量距離。

vocab.ex: Measure the line with a ruler.
vocab.exzh: 用尺量這條線。

vocab.ex: A large-scale map shows more detail.
vocab.exzh: 大比例尺的地圖畫得比較詳細。

quiz.q: Where do you look to find out what a map symbol means?
On most maps, which direction is at the top?
At a scale of 1:25,000, how far on the ground is 4 cm on the map?
Which map shows a small area in great detail?
Which way is halfway between north and east?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: A map is a view from above
parts.text_en: Watch the camera turn until it looks straight down. The buildings and trees fade, and symbols take their place.
parts.text_zh: 看鏡頭慢慢轉到正上方。房子和樹淡出，換成符號。

parts.text_en: The school is highlighted on the map and in the legend. Click other symbols in the legend to find them too.
parts.text_zh: 學校在地圖上和圖例裡都亮了起來。點圖例裡的其他符號，也找找看。

parts.text_en: Zoom to the neighborhood. The view is 1 km wide instead of 10 km, so a 20 cm print would be 1:5,000. Watch the scale bar change.
parts.text_zh: 拉近到街區。畫面寬 1 公里而不是 10 公里，印成 20 公分寬就是 1:5,000。注意圖形比例尺怎麼改變。

parts.text_en: The island turns halfway around. The north arrow in the corner turns with it, so you can always tell which way is north.
parts.text_zh: 小島轉了半圈，角落的北方箭頭也跟著轉，所以你永遠知道哪邊是北。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Turn the island until north points to the right. Which place is now at the top of the screen?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。把小島轉到北方箭頭指向右邊。現在畫面最上方是哪個地方？

measure.lead_en: Drag the ends of the ruler, A and B. The page imagines this map printed 20 cm wide and works out the scale: the whole island is 1:50,000, the town is 1:12,500, and the neighborhood is 1:5,000. Read the ruler in centimeters, multiply by the scale, and you have the distance on the ground. Try the same two places at different scales: the ground distance stays the same, but the ruler changes.
measure.lead_zh: 拖動尺的兩端 A、B。頁面假設這張地圖印成 20 公分寬，算出比例尺：整座島是 1:50,000，小鎮是 1:12,500，街區是 1:5,000。讀出尺上的公分數，乘上比例尺，就是地面上的距離。用不同的比例尺量同樣兩個地方試試：地面上的距離不變，尺上的數字卻變了。

legend.en: Find Your Way on the Map
legend.lead_en: Eight questions about the same imaginary island. Each one starts at the place circled in pink. Use the north arrow, the scale bar, and the symbols to answer. There is no timer, and the game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
legend.lead_zh: 同一座虛構小島的八個問題。每一題都從粉紅色圈起來的地方出發。用北方箭頭、圖形比例尺和符號回答。不計時，遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。
legend.start_en: North is at the top of this map. Find the start, then look in the direction the question asks.
legend.start_zh: 這張地圖上方是北。先找到起點，再往題目說的方向看。
legend.end_en: Scale, direction, and legend: with these three, any map will answer your questions.
legend.end_zh: 比例尺、方位、圖例：有了這三樣，任何一張地圖都會回答你的問題。

toward.en: Put your finger on the start and slide it in that direction. Which symbol do you reach first?
toward.zh: 手指放在起點，往那個方向滑。最先碰到哪個符號？

dir.en: North is up, east is right. Is the place up or down from the start? Left or right?
dir.zh: 上方是北、右邊是東。那個地方在起點的上面還是下面？左邊還是右邊？

trail.en: Follow the red dashed line from the start. Which symbol sits on it first?
trail.zh: 從起點沿著紅色虛線走。最先遇到哪個符號？

closer.en: Compare the two straight lines from the start. The scale bar can help.
closer.zh: 比較從起點出發的兩條直線哪一條短；圖形比例尺可以幫忙。

dist.en: Lay the edge of a piece of paper along the scale bar, mark 1 km, then step it along the line.
dist.zh: 拿紙邊對著圖形比例尺標出 1 公里，再沿著那條線一段一段量。

flow.en: Rivers flow downhill toward the sea. Where does this river meet the coast?
flow.zh: 河往低處流向海。這條河在哪裡碰到海岸？

questions.en: Start at the school and walk due east. Which place do you reach?
questions.zh: 從學校出發，一直往正東走。會走到哪裡？
questions.why_en: East is to the right on this map. The harbor is straight to the right of the school, about 2 km away.
questions.why_zh: 這張地圖右邊是東。港口就在學校的正右方，大約 2 公里。

questions.en: Start at the lighthouse and go north along the road. Which is the first place you reach?
questions.zh: 從燈塔出發，沿著公路往北走。最先會到哪裡？
questions.why_en: The road from the lighthouse runs north to the bridge over the river.
questions.why_zh: 從燈塔出發的公路往北通到河上的那座橋。

questions.en: From the harbor, in which direction is the summit?
questions.zh: 從港口看，山頂在哪個方向？
questions.why_en: The summit is straight up from the harbor on the map, so it is due north.
questions.why_zh: 在地圖上，山頂在港口的正上方，所以是正北。

questions.en: You are at the bridge. In which direction is the school?
questions.zh: 你在橋上。學校在哪個方向？
questions.why_en: The school is up and to the left of the bridge: north and west, so northwest.
questions.why_zh: 學校在橋的左上方：偏北又偏西，所以是西北。

questions.en: Start at the trailhead and follow the hiking trail uphill. What is the first place on the trail?
questions.zh: 從登山口出發，沿著登山步道往上走。步道上最先遇到的是什麼？
questions.why_en: The red dashed trail reaches the mountain hut about halfway, before it reaches the summit.
questions.why_zh: 紅色虛線的步道大約走到一半就到山屋，然後才到山頂。

questions.en: Which is closer to the school in a straight line: the temple or the harbor?
questions.zh: 直線距離，哪一個離學校比較近：廟還是港口？
questions.why_en: The temple is less than 1 km from the school. The harbor is about 2 km away.
questions.why_zh: 廟離學校不到 1 公里；港口大約 2 公里。

questions.en: Use the scale bar. About how far is it in a straight line from the bridge to the lighthouse?
questions.zh: 用圖形比例尺。從橋到燈塔，直線距離大約多遠？
questions.why_en: The straight line is a little less than twice the 1 km bar, about 1.7 km.
questions.why_zh: 那條直線比兩段 1 公里的比例尺短一點，大約 1.7 公里。

questions.en: At the bridge, which way does the river flow?
questions.zh: 在橋那裡，河往哪個方向流？
questions.why_en: The river starts on the mountain in the north and flows south, downhill, to the sea.
questions.why_zh: 河從北邊的山上流下來，往南、往低處流到海裡。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for finding your way
map_english.zh: 找路時用得到的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about direction and distance. Listen, repeat, then give a partner directions on the island map.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說方位和距離。先聽、再跟著唸，然後在小島的地圖上幫同伴指路。

items.en: The school is northeast of the temple.
items.zh: 學校在廟的東北方。

items.en: One centimeter on this map stands for five hundred meters.
items.zh: 這張地圖上的一公分代表五百公尺。

items.en: Turn left after the bridge.
items.zh: 過了橋之後左轉。

items.en: The legend shows what each symbol means.
items.zh: 圖例說明每個符號代表什麼。

items.en: The harbor is about two kilometers away.
items.zh: 港口大約在兩公里外。

items.en: Go straight along the road until you reach the river.
items.zh: 沿著公路直走，走到河邊。

items.en: The lighthouse is at the southern end of the island.
items.zh: 燈塔在島的南端。
items.use_en: at the northern / southern end of

items.en: Which way is north on this map?
items.zh: 這張地圖上哪邊是北？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Map · 地圖背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: East at the top, Taiwan's map symbols, three norths, and a common mistake
culture_cards.title_zh: 上方是東方的地圖、台灣地形圖的符號、三種北，和一個常見的錯誤
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how maps show direction, symbols, and scale.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，講地圖怎麼表示方位、符號和比例尺。

cards.en: When east was at the top
cards.body_en: North was not always at the top. A world map of 1532 from the tradition of medieval “T-in-O” maps puts east at the top, according to an exhibit at the Newberry Library in Chicago. The same exhibit explains that north probably moved to the top because sailors could rely on the North Star, and, after about 1450, because compasses, which point north, came into wide use.
cards.body_zh: 北方不是一直都在上面。依美國芝加哥紐伯里圖書館的展覽說明，一張 1532 年、屬於中世紀「T-O 地圖」傳統的世界地圖，上方是東方。展覽也說明，北方後來會跑到上面，可能是因為航海的人可以依靠北極星，而且大約 1450 年以後指向北方的羅盤普遍了起來。

cards.en: A flag for a school, an anchor for a harbor
cards.zh: 學校是一面旗，港口是一個錨
cards.body_en: Taiwan's 1:25,000 topographic maps, made by the National Land Surveying and Mapping Center, have a legend with dozens of symbols. A school is a small flag on a pole, a harbor is an anchor, and a lighthouse is a small star of rays. The symbols on this page were drawn for this lesson. They look similar, but they are not the official ones.
cards.body_zh: 內政部國土測繪中心的 1/25,000 經建版地形圖，圖例裡有好幾十種符號：學校是一面插在竿子上的小旗子，港口是一個錨，燈塔是一個放射光芒的小星形。本頁的符號是為這一課自己畫的，樣子相近，但不是官方的符號。

cards.en: Which north does a compass find?
cards.zh: 指北針找到的是哪一個北？
cards.body_en: There is more than one north. True north points along a line of longitude to the North Pole. Grid north follows the grid printed on the map. Magnetic north is where a compass needle points, and it changes slowly with place and time. In Taipei a compass points about 5 degrees west of true north, according to NOAA's calculator for October 2026. Each sheet of Taiwan's topographic maps prints a small diagram of the three norths; one sheet from 2020 shows 4 degrees 44 minutes between grid north and magnetic north.
cards.body_zh: 北方不只一種。真北是沿著經線指向北極的方向；方格北是地圖上印的方格的方向；磁北是指北針的針所指的方向，而且會隨地點和時間慢慢改變。依美國國家海洋暨大氣總署（NOAA）的計算器，2026 年 10 月在台北，指北針大約指向真北偏西 5 度。台灣的地形圖每一幅都印著一張小小的「偏角圖」；其中一幅 2020 年的圖，方格北和磁北之間是 4 度 44 分。

cards.en: A mistake the curriculum warns about
cards.zh: 課綱特別提醒的一個錯誤
cards.body_en: Map scales are taught in grade 6 math in Taiwan. The curriculum asks teachers to deal with a common mistake: thinking that a bigger number after the 1 means a bigger drawing. In fact, 1:50,000 draws the same road half as long as 1:25,000. Try it with the ruler on this page by switching between the island and the town.
cards.body_zh: 台灣在國小六年級的數學課教地圖比例尺。課綱特別要老師處理一個常見的錯誤：以為「比例分母愈大，相對邊長也愈大」。其實 1:50,000 畫出來的同一條路，長度只有 1:25,000 的一半。用本頁的尺，在「整座島」和「小鎮」之間切換試試看。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum (2018). Map scale appears in grade 6 math. In social studies, the elementary and junior high content has no entry about map symbols or directions; maps appear in senior high geography.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要（民國 107 年發布）。地圖比例尺出現在國小六年級的數學；社會領域的國小、國中學習內容沒有談地圖符號或方位的條目，地圖要到高中地理才出現。

items.text: 解題：地圖比例尺。地圖比例尺之意義、記號與應用。地圖上兩邊長的比和實際兩邊長的比相等。
items.note_en: The “Measure It” activity is this entry in action: read the ruler, multiply by the scale, and compare scales. The curriculum notes the common mistake of thinking a bigger denominator means a longer line on the map.
items.note_zh: 「量一量」就是這一條的實作：讀尺、乘上比例尺、比較不同的比例尺。課綱的備註提醒要處理「以為比例分母愈大，相對邊長也愈大」的常見錯誤。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.text: 地圖本質與要素。
items.note_en: Scale, direction, and legend are the elements every map needs.
items.note_zh: 比例尺、方位、圖例，是每一張地圖都要有的要素。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.text: 問題探究：地圖判讀與使用。
items.note_en: “Find Your Way on the Map” practices reading a map to answer questions about direction and distance.
items.note_zh: 「照著地圖找」練習的，就是讀地圖來回答方位和距離的問題。

myths.myth_en: North is always at the top of a map.
myths.myth_zh: 地圖的上方一定是北方。
myths.fact_en: Most maps today put north at the top, but not all of them. Always check the north arrow. National Geographic's teaching guide lists this as a common misconception.
myths.fact_zh: 今天大多數的地圖上方是北，但不是全部。一定要看北方箭頭。國家地理學會的教學指引也把這一點列為常見的誤解。

myths.myth_en: A large-scale map shows a large area.
myths.myth_zh: 大比例尺的地圖，畫的範圍很大。
myths.fact_en: It is the other way around. A large-scale map, such as 1:5,000, shows a small area in great detail. The larger the second number, the smaller the scale.
myths.fact_zh: 剛好相反。大比例尺的地圖（例如 1:5,000）畫的是小範圍、細節很多。比例尺的第二個數字越大，比例尺就越小。

myths.myth_en: A map symbol means the same thing on every map.
myths.myth_zh: 同一個符號在每一張地圖上的意思都一樣。
myths.fact_en: Each map chooses its own symbols. On older U.S. Geological Survey maps, one small symbol stood for both a school and a house of worship; on Taiwan's topographic maps a school is a small flag. That is why every map needs its own legend.
myths.fact_zh: 每一張地圖自己決定用什麼符號。美國地質調查所的舊地形圖上，學校和教堂共用同一個符號；台灣的地形圖上，學校是一面小旗子。所以每一張地圖都需要自己的圖例。

myths.myth_en: If you enlarge a map on a copier, its scale of 1:25,000 is still right.
myths.myth_zh: 用影印機把地圖放大，上面寫的 1:25,000 還是對的。
myths.fact_en: The number is no longer right, because every distance on the copy has grown. The scale bar grows with the map, so it is still correct. The same is true when you zoom in on a screen.
myths.fact_zh: 那個數字已經不對了，因為影本上每一段距離都變長了。圖形比例尺跟著地圖一起放大，所以仍然正確。在螢幕上放大地圖也是一樣。

tricks_head.en: Reading a map in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住怎麼看地圖

tricks.body_en: Three things to find before you read anything else on a map.
tricks.body_zh: 看地圖上任何東西之前，先找這三樣。

tricks.body_en: North, East, South, West, going clockwise. The first letters spell the English saying.
tricks.body_zh: 從北開始順時針轉一圈：北、東、南、西。英文的四個字首剛好是 Never Eat Soggy Waffles。

tricks.body_en: A large-scale map shows a small area in great detail.
tricks.body_zh: 大比例尺的地圖，畫的範圍小、細節多。

tricks.body_en: If a map is enlarged or shrunk, the scale bar changes size with it, so it stays right.
tricks.body_zh: 地圖放大或縮小時，圖形比例尺跟著一起變，所以永遠是對的。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: When you walk around the school to measure, walk, do not run, and stay where your teacher can see you.
safety.zh: 在校園裡走動測量時，用走的、不要跑，並待在老師看得到的地方。

safety.en: Do not count paces on stairs, near a road, or near the edge of a pond.
safety.zh: 不要在樓梯、馬路邊或水池邊數步數。

safety.en: Keep the measuring tape low and do not let it snap back toward anyone's face.
safety.zh: 捲尺拉低一點，收回時不要讓它彈向任何人的臉。

safety.en: If you use a compass, keep it away from phones, magnets, and metal desks, which can pull the needle off.
safety.zh: 使用指北針時，遠離手機、磁鐵和鐵桌，它們會讓指針偏掉。

materials.en: Graph paper with 1 cm squares
A measuring tape
A pencil, an eraser, and colored pencils
A compass, or a phone compass checked by the teacher
materials.zh: 一個指北針，或老師確認過的手機指南針

steps.en: Measure the length and width of the classroom with the tape.
steps.zh: 用捲尺量教室的長和寬。

steps.en: Choose a scale so the room fits on the paper, for example 1 square = 50 cm. Write it as a scale: 1 cm = 50 cm, or 1:50.
steps.zh: 選一個比例尺，讓教室畫得進這張紙，例如一格＝50 公分。寫成比例尺：1 公分＝50 公分，也就是 1:50。

steps.en: Draw the walls, the door, the windows, and the teacher's desk to scale.
steps.zh: 照比例畫出牆、門、窗和講桌。

steps.en: Make up a symbol for each kind of thing, such as desks, cabinets, and plants, and put them in a legend.
steps.zh: 幫每一種東西想一個符號（例如課桌、櫃子、盆栽），寫進圖例。

steps.en: Find north with the compass and draw a north arrow. Then trade maps with a partner and find each other's seats.
steps.zh: 用指北針找出北方，畫上北方箭頭。然後和同伴交換地圖，找出對方的座位。

activities.tip_en: A classroom map at 1:50 is a very large-scale map: each desk can be drawn. A map of the whole school on the same paper would need a smaller scale and simpler symbols.
activities.tip_zh: 1:50 的教室地圖是很大比例尺的地圖，每張桌子都畫得出來。同一張紙要畫整座學校，就得用比較小的比例尺和比較簡單的符號。

materials.en: A measuring tape
A simple map of the playground drawn by the teacher, with a north arrow
materials.zh: 老師畫的操場簡圖，上面有北方箭頭

materials.en: A small object to hide, such as a beanbag
materials.zh: 一個要藏起來的小東西，例如沙包

steps.en: Measure 10 meters with the tape. Walk it normally and count your steps. Divide 10 by your number of steps to find the length of one of your paces.
steps.zh: 用捲尺量出 10 公尺，用平常的步伐走過去，數一數走了幾步。10 除以步數，就是你一步的長度。

steps.en: One team hides the object and writes directions using the map: “From the flagpole, walk 30 paces north, then 12 paces east.”
steps.zh: 一組把東西藏起來，對著地圖寫下指示：「從旗桿出發，往北走 30 步，再往東走 12 步。」

steps.en: Mark the hiding place on the map with a symbol and add it to the legend.
steps.zh: 在地圖上用一個符號標出藏東西的地方，並加進圖例。

steps.en: Another team follows the directions to find it. Did their paces match yours?
steps.zh: 另一組照著指示去找。他們的步數和你們的對得上嗎？

steps.en: Rewrite the directions in meters instead of paces. Which version works for everyone?
steps.zh: 把指示改寫成公尺，而不是步數。哪一種寫法每個人都能用？

activities.tip_en: Paces are a scale that changes from person to person. Meters are the same for everyone, which is why maps use them.
activities.tip_zh: 步數是一種因人而異的「比例尺」；公尺對每個人都一樣，所以地圖用公尺。

links_head.en: The rest of Unit 1, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 單元一的其他課，以及下一課

links.en: Why Is Every Flat Map Wrong?
links.zh: 為什麼每一張平面地圖都是「錯」的？
links.note_en: A small town map hardly needs a projection, but a world map does, and its scale changes from place to place.
links.note_zh: 小鎮的地圖幾乎不用管投影，世界地圖就要了，而且它的比例尺每個地方都不一樣。

links.en: How Do You Find Any Place on Earth?
links.zh: 怎麼找到地球上任何一個地方？
links.note_en: On a globe, north is always along a line of longitude, toward the North Pole.
links.note_zh: 在地球儀上，北方永遠是沿著經線、朝北極的方向。

links.en: How Do You Draw a Mountain on Flat Paper?
links.zh: 怎麼在平面上畫出一座山？
links.note_en: The thin brown lines on today's map are contour lines. That lesson shows how to read them.
links.note_zh: 今天這張地圖上細細的褐色線就是等高線，那一課教你怎麼讀。

links.en: Why Is It Night in New York When It Is Day in Taipei?
links.zh: 台北是白天，紐約為什麼是晚上？
links.note_en: Unit 2 begins with time zones: the Earth turns, and the time of day travels around it.
links.note_zh: 單元二從時區開始：地球在轉，一天的時間跟著繞地球一圈。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The island, the town, its distances and directions, and the answers to the game are made and computed by the page itself and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；小島、小鎮、距離、方位與小遊戲的答案都由頁面自己產生與計算，並有自動測試

sources.en: “Scale is the relationship between distance on the map and distance on the ground”; “the larger the second number is, the smaller the scale of the map”; small-scale maps (1:250,000 and smaller) show large areas.
sources.zh: 比例尺是地圖距離和地面距離的關係；第二個數字越大，比例尺越小；1:250,000 以下是小比例尺
sources.src: U.S. Geological Survey, Fact Sheet 015-02, “Map Scales” (2002)

sources.en: At 1:25,000, “every 1cm on the map represents 25 000 … on the ground (for example, 25 000cm = 250 metres)”; Ordnance Survey maps are printed with north at the top; measure with string against the scale bar.
sources.zh: 1:25,000 地圖上 1 公分＝地面 250 公尺；英國地形測量局的地圖北方在上；用繩子對著比例尺量
sources.src: Ordnance Survey, “Map reading made easy”

sources.en: On maps reduced or enlarged by photocopying, the original ratio and written scales are incorrect, but a graphic scale enlarged or reduced with the map “is still correct.”
sources.zh: 影印放大或縮小後，數字與文字比例尺不再正確，圖形比例尺仍然正確

sources.en: A legend, “sometimes called a ‘key,’” lists a map's symbols, lines, and colors; a compass rose or an arrow shows direction.
sources.zh: 圖例（key）列出地圖的符號、線條和顏色；指北的箭頭或羅盤分劃圖表示方位

sources.en: “Students may have the misconception that north is always at the ‘top.’”

sources.en: Cardinal directions and the intermediate points such as northeast and southeast.
sources.zh: 四個主要方位與東北、東南等中間方位

sources.en: The 1532 Mappamundi of Isidore of Seville has an east-up orientation from the “T-in-O” tradition; north-up likely came from the direction of Polaris and, after 1450, the use of the compass.
sources.zh: 1532 年的世界地圖上方是東方；北方在上可能源自北極星與 1450 年後羅盤的普及
sources.src: Newberry Library, “The Occidental Tourist: 500 Years of Orienting Maps”

sources.en: True north, grid north, and magnetic north on topographic maps.
sources.zh: 地形圖上的真北、方格北與磁北

sources.en: Magnetic declination is “the angle between magnetic north and true north” and changes with place and time; for Taipei on October 16, 2026, the World Magnetic Model gives about 5.06° west.
sources.zh: 磁偏角是磁北與真北的夾角，隨地點與時間改變；2026 年 10 月 16 日台北約為西偏 5.06 度（WMM 2025）
sources.src: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Magnetic Field Calculators

sources.en: The U.S. Geological Survey's map symbol booklet combines “School; house of worship” in one symbol.
sources.zh: 美國地質調查所的地圖符號手冊裡，學校與教堂共用一個符號

units.blurb_en: Time zones, continents and oceans, hot and cold places, and where people live.
units.blurb_zh: 時區、大洲與大洋、熱的地方和冷的地方，以及人都住在哪裡。

lessons.title: Why Is It Night in New York When It Is Day in Taipei?
lessons.title_zh: 台北是白天，紐約為什麼是晚上？
lessons.blurb_en: Turn a 3D Earth under a fixed Sun and watch day and night sweep around it. See why clocks are set by time zones, what happens at the International Date Line, and work out what time it is on the other side of the world.
lessons.blurb_zh: 讓 3D 地球在固定的太陽下轉，看白天和黑夜繞著地球移動。了解鐘為什麼照時區來調、國際換日線發生什麼事，再算算地球另一邊現在幾點。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Earth turns once a day, 15 degrees every hour, so the Sun is overhead at different places at different times. People divide the Earth into time zones so that clocks in one zone agree. Crossing the International Date Line changes the date by one day.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 地球一天轉一圈、每小時轉 15 度，所以太陽在不同的時間照到不同的地方的正上方。人把地球分成時區，讓同一區的鐘一致。跨過國際換日線，日期就差一天。

lab.title_en: The Earth Turns Under the Sun
lab.how_en: The Sun shines from the right and stays there. Press “Turn the Earth,” or drag the time slider, and the Earth turns from west to east. The gold line is the edge between day and night. The cities show the time on their clocks. Turn on the bands to see idealized time zones, one every 15 degrees, and the red line for the idealized date line. Real time zone borders are not drawn.
lab.how_zh: 太陽從右邊照過來，而且不動。按「讓地球轉」或拖動時間滑桿，地球由西向東轉。金色的線是白天和黑夜的交界。城市旁邊顯示當地鐘上的時間。打開時區帶，可以看到每 15 度一條的理想時區，紅色的線是理想的換日線。真實的時區界線沒有畫出來。

legend.en: The edge between day and night

legend.zh: 理想時區，每區寬 15 度

legend.en: The idealized date line at 180 degrees
legend.zh: 理想的換日線（180 度經線）

lab.scale_en: One second of the animation is one and a half hours. The Sun's direction is fixed; the seasons buttons tilt it north or south to show how the edge between day and night tilts too.
lab.scale_zh: 動畫的一秒是一個半小時。太陽的方向固定不動；季節按鈕讓陽光偏北或偏南，看晝夜交界也跟著傾斜。
lab.credit_html: Land outlines: Natural Earth, 1:50m Land, version 5.1.2, public domain. City positions are rounded to one-tenth of a degree. Times are for idealized time zones without daylight saving time. · 陸地外形：Natural Earth 1:50m Land 5.1.2 版，公有領域。城市位置取到 0.1 度。時間是理想時區，不含夏令時間。

paras: Suppose you call a friend in New York at three o'clock on a sunny afternoon in Taipei. Your friend answers sleepily, because in New York it is two o'clock in the morning. You are both talking at the same moment, yet one of you is in the afternoon and the other is in the middle of the night. How can that be?

The answer is that the Earth is turning. It spins once a day, from west to east, so the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west. At any moment, about half of the Earth faces the Sun and has day, and the other half faces away and has night. Because a full turn is 360 degrees and a day is 24 hours, the Earth turns 15 degrees every hour.

Long ago, every town set its clocks by its own Sun: noon was when the Sun was highest. That worked when people traveled slowly. But when trains began to cross whole countries, every station had a slightly different time, and timetables became confusing. So people agreed on standard time: everyone in a large area uses the same clock time, even if the Sun is not exactly overhead at noon.

Today the world is divided into time zones. The simplest picture is 24 zones, each 15 degrees wide, one hour apart. Time is counted from the prime meridian at Greenwich, using Coordinated Universal Time, or UTC. Taiwan's national standard time is UTC plus 8 hours, and New York uses UTC minus 5 hours in winter and minus 4 in summer. Real time zone borders are not straight lines. They bend to follow the borders of countries and regions, and some places even use half hours.

If you keep moving east through the time zones, your clock keeps moving forward. Go all the way around the world and you would gain a whole day. To fix this, people use the International Date Line, which runs roughly along the 180-degree meridian in the Pacific Ocean. When you cross it going west, the date jumps forward one day. When you cross it going east, the date goes back one day.

So when it is Monday afternoon in Taipei, it can still be Monday morning in London, very early Monday in New York, and Sunday evening in Los Angeles. Before you call someone far away, do a little geography: find their time zone, count the hours, and make sure you will not wake them up.
paras_zh: 假設台北一個晴朗的下午三點，你打電話給在紐約的朋友。朋友睡眼惺忪地接起來，因為紐約是凌晨兩點。你們在同一個瞬間說話，一個人在下午、另一個人卻在半夜。這是怎麼回事？
答案是：地球在轉。地球一天自轉一圈，由西向東轉，所以太陽看起來從東邊升起、從西邊落下。任何時候，地球大約有一半面對太陽，是白天；另一半背對太陽，是黑夜。轉一整圈是 360 度，一天是 24 小時，所以地球每小時轉 15 度。
很久以前，每個城鎮照自己的太陽來調鐘：太陽最高的時候就是正午。人走得慢的時候這樣沒問題。可是火車開始橫越整個國家以後，每一站的時間都差一點，時刻表就亂了。所以人們約定了標準時間：一大片地區的人都用同一個鐘點，就算太陽不是剛好在正午時最高也沒關係。
今天，世界被分成好幾個時區。最簡單的畫法是 24 個時區，每區寬 15 度，相鄰兩區差一小時。時間從格林威治的本初子午線算起，用的是協調世界時（UTC）。台灣的「國家標準時間」是 UTC 加 8 小時；紐約冬天用 UTC 減 5 小時，夏天用 UTC 減 4 小時。真實的時區界線不是直線，會跟著國家和地區的邊界彎曲，有些地方甚至用半小時。
如果一直往東走、穿過一個又一個時區，你的鐘就要一直往前調。繞地球一整圈，你就多出了一整天。為了解決這個問題，人們用一條國際換日線，大致沿著太平洋上的 180 度經線。往西跨過它，日期往前跳一天；往東跨過它，日期退回一天。
所以當台北是星期一下午，倫敦可能還是星期一早上，紐約是星期一清晨，洛杉磯則還是星期日晚上。打電話給遠方的人之前，先做一點地理：找出對方的時區、算算差幾小時，確定不會把人吵醒。
questions: Why does the Earth turn 15 degrees every hour?
Why did people start using standard time instead of each town's own Sun time?
You fly west across the International Date Line on Tuesday. What day is it right after you cross?
answers: A full turn is 360 degrees and it takes 24 hours, and 360 divided by 24 is 15.
When trains connected faraway towns, every station having its own slightly different time made timetables confusing. Agreeing on one clock time for a large area solved that.
Wednesday. Crossing the line going west moves the date forward one day.

vocab.ex: Taipei and Tokyo are in different time zones.
vocab.exzh: 台北和東京在不同的時區。

vocab.ex: The Earth rotates from west to east.
vocab.exzh: 地球由西向東自轉。

vocab.ex: At noon the Sun is at its highest point.
vocab.exzh: 正午時太陽在最高的位置。

vocab.ex: It is midnight in New York when it is noon in Taipei.
vocab.exzh: 台北正午時，紐約是午夜。

vocab.ex: Taipei is thirteen hours ahead of New York in winter.
vocab.exzh: 冬天時，台北比紐約快十三小時。

vocab.ex: London is eight hours behind Taipei.
vocab.exzh: 倫敦比台北慢八小時。

vocab.ex: We crossed the date line and lost a day.
vocab.exzh: 我們跨過換日線，少了一天。

vocab.ex: Railways helped the world agree on standard time.
vocab.exzh: 鐵路幫助世界約定了標準時間。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: The Earth turns, the Sun stays
parts.text_en: Watch the Earth turn from west to east under a Sun that does not move. Each city passes from night into day at the gold line.
parts.text_zh: 看地球在不動的太陽下由西向東轉。每個城市在金色的線那裡從黑夜進入白天。

parts.en: Afternoon in Taipei, night in New York
parts.text_en: At 6:00 UTC it is 2 p.m. in Taipei and 1 a.m. in New York: the two cities are on opposite sides of the Earth.
parts.text_zh: 協調世界時 6 點，台北是下午 2 點、紐約是凌晨 1 點：兩個城市在地球的兩邊。

parts.text_en: At 20:00 UTC on Monday, Taipei and Sydney are already in Tuesday, while Los Angeles is still on Monday. Check the dates in the list.
parts.text_zh: 星期一協調世界時 20 點，台北和雪梨已經是星期二，洛杉磯還是星期一。看看右邊清單上的日期。

parts.en: The line between day and night tilts
parts.text_en: In June the Sun shines more on the north, so the gold line tilts and the North Pole stays in daylight all day.
parts.text_zh: 六月時陽光偏向北邊，金色的線傾斜了，北極整天都在白天裡。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Find a time when Taipei and London are both in daylight. How many hours of overlap can you find?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。找一個台北和倫敦都是白天的時間。兩邊同時是白天的時間有幾個小時？

clock.lead_en: Eight questions. Each one gives the day and time in Taipei and asks for the time in another place. Use idealized time zones: one hour for every 15 degrees of longitude, with no daylight saving time. There is no timer, and the game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
clock.lead_zh: 八道題。每一題給台北的星期和時間，問另一個地方幾點。用理想時區來算：經度每 15 度差一小時，不算夏令時間。不計時，遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。
clock.hint_en: First find the place's time zone: divide its longitude by 15 and round. Taipei is +8. Then count the difference, and watch for midnight.
clock.hint_zh: 先找出那個地方的時區：經度除以 15 再四捨五入。台北是 +8。再算兩邊差幾小時，注意有沒有跨過半夜。
clock.start_en: East of Taipei is later; west of Taipei is earlier.
clock.start_zh: 在台北東邊的地方比較晚（鐘比較快）；在西邊的比較早。
clock.end_en: Count the zones, mind midnight, and you can work out the time anywhere on Earth.
clock.end_zh: 數時區、注意半夜，就能算出地球上任何地方的時間。

questions.en: Monday, 3 p.m. in Taipei. What time is it in New York?
questions.zh: 台北星期一下午 3 點，紐約幾點？
questions.why_en: New York is UTC−5 and Taipei is UTC+8, a difference of 13 hours. 3 p.m. minus 13 hours is 2 a.m. the same day.
questions.why_zh: 紐約是 UTC−5、台北是 UTC+8，差 13 小時。下午 3 點減 13 小時，是同一天的凌晨 2 點。

questions.en: Monday, 3 p.m. in Taipei. What time is it in London?
questions.zh: 台北星期一下午 3 點，倫敦幾點？
questions.why_en: London is on the prime meridian, UTC+0, eight hours behind Taipei. 3 p.m. minus 8 hours is 7 a.m.
questions.why_zh: 倫敦在本初子午線上，是 UTC+0，比台北慢 8 小時。下午 3 點減 8 小時是早上 7 點。

questions.en: Tuesday, 8 a.m. in Taipei. What time is it in Los Angeles?
questions.zh: 台北星期二早上 8 點，洛杉磯幾點？
questions.why_en: Los Angeles is UTC−8, sixteen hours behind Taipei. Going back 16 hours from Tuesday 8 a.m. lands on Monday 4 p.m.
questions.why_zh: 洛杉磯是 UTC−8，比台北慢 16 小時。從星期二早上 8 點往回 16 小時，是星期一下午 4 點。

questions.en: Sunday, 11 p.m. in Taipei. What time is it in Sydney?
questions.zh: 台北星期日晚上 11 點，雪梨幾點？
questions.why_en: Sydney is UTC+10, two hours ahead. Two hours after Sunday 11 p.m. is Monday 1 a.m.
questions.why_zh: 雪梨是 UTC+10，比台北快 2 小時。星期日晚上 11 點再過 2 小時，是星期一凌晨 1 點。

questions.en: Wednesday, noon in Taipei. What time is it in Tokyo?
questions.zh: 台北星期三中午 12 點，東京幾點？
questions.why_en: Tokyo is UTC+9, one hour ahead of Taipei, so it is 1 p.m.
questions.why_zh: 東京是 UTC+9，比台北快 1 小時，所以是下午 1 點。

questions.en: Friday, 9 a.m. in Taipei. What time is it at 30 degrees east?
questions.zh: 台北星期五早上 9 點，東經 30 度是幾點？
questions.why_en: 30 divided by 15 is 2, so that zone is UTC+2, six hours behind Taipei. 9 a.m. minus 6 hours is 3 a.m.
questions.why_zh: 30 除以 15 是 2，那一區是 UTC+2，比台北慢 6 小時。早上 9 點減 6 小時是凌晨 3 點。

questions.en: Monday, 10 a.m. in Taipei. What time is it at 120 degrees west?
questions.zh: 台北星期一早上 10 點，西經 120 度是幾點？
questions.why_en: That zone is UTC−8, sixteen hours behind Taipei. Going back 16 hours from Monday 10 a.m. gives Sunday 6 p.m.
questions.why_zh: 那一區是 UTC−8，比台北慢 16 小時。從星期一早上 10 點往回 16 小時，是星期日下午 6 點。

questions.en: Thursday, 6 p.m. in Taipei. What time is it in Rio de Janeiro?
questions.zh: 台北星期四晚上 6 點，里約熱內盧幾點？
questions.why_en: Rio de Janeiro is about 43 degrees west, so its idealized zone is UTC−3, eleven hours behind Taipei. 6 p.m. minus 11 hours is 7 a.m.
questions.why_zh: 里約熱內盧大約在西經 43 度，理想時區是 UTC−3，比台北慢 11 小時。晚上 6 點減 11 小時是早上 7 點。

call.en: Before You Call, Check the Clock
call.lead_en: Slide the time in Taipei and choose who you are calling. The two clocks show both times side by side. This uses idealized time zones without daylight saving time, so check a real clock before an important call.
call.lead_zh: 拉動台北的時間，再選要打給哪裡。兩個鐘並排顯示兩邊的時間。這裡用理想時區、不算夏令時間，重要的電話打之前，還是要查一下真的時間。
call.msg_sleep_en: They are probably asleep. Wait a few hours, or send a message instead.
call.msg_sleep_zh: 對方大概在睡覺。等幾個小時，或改傳訊息。
call.msg_edge_en: It is early morning or late evening there. A short call might be all right, but ask first.
call.msg_edge_zh: 那裡是清晨或深夜。簡短的電話也許可以，但先問一下比較好。
call.msg_ok_en: It is daytime there. A good time to call.
call.msg_ok_zh: 那裡是白天，是打電話的好時間。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about time
map_english.zh: 談時間與時區的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about time. Listen, repeat, then ask a partner what time it is in a city of your choice.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說時間。先聽、再跟著唸，然後問同伴你選的城市現在幾點。

items.en: It is three in the afternoon in Taipei.
items.zh: 台北現在是下午三點。

items.en: New York is thirteen hours behind Taipei in winter.
items.zh: 冬天時，紐約比台北慢十三小時。

items.en: What time is it in London right now?
items.zh: 倫敦現在幾點？
items.use_en: What time is it in … right now?

items.en: Taiwan is in the UTC plus eight time zone.
items.zh: 台灣在 UTC+8 時區。

items.en: The Earth turns from west to east.
items.zh: 地球由西向東轉。

items.en: When we cross the date line, the date changes.
items.zh: 跨過換日線時，日期就改變了。

items.en: It is already Tuesday in Sydney.
items.zh: 雪梨已經是星期二了。

items.en: Let's call them after school, when it is morning there.
items.zh: 我們放學後再打給他們，那時他們那邊是早上。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Clocks · 鐘背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: The day of two noons, Greenwich time, Taiwan's clocks, and a lost day
culture_cards.title_zh: 兩個正午的一天、格林威治的時間、台灣的鐘，和消失的一天
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people agreed on what time it is.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，講人怎麼對「現在幾點」取得共識。

cards.body_en: Before 1883, North American railroads ran on many local times. On November 18, 1883, station clocks were reset to a new standard time as noon arrived in each zone. Many towns heard noon twice that day, once by the old Sun time and once by the new standard time, so the Library of Congress calls it the Day of Two Noons.
cards.body_zh: 1883 年以前，北美的鐵路用的是許多不同的地方時間。1883 年 11 月 18 日，各時區到了正午，車站的鐘就被重新調成新的標準時間。很多城鎮那天過了兩次正午：一次照舊的太陽時，一次照新的標準時間，所以美國國會圖書館稱這一天為「兩個正午的一天」。

cards.zh: 從格林威治時間到協調世界時
cards.body_en: Greenwich Mean Time is the average clock time at Greenwich. Today the world's reference is Coordinated Universal Time, UTC, which the Royal Observatory describes as the modern equivalent of GMT, never more than half a second different from it. UTC is kept by comparing atomic clocks around the world; the International Bureau of Weights and Measures in France combines their results.
cards.body_zh: 格林威治標準時間是格林威治的平均鐘點時間。今天全世界的參考時間是協調世界時（UTC）；格林威治皇家天文台說它是格林威治標準時間的現代版本，兩者相差從來不超過半秒。協調世界時是比較世界各地的原子鐘得出來的，由設在法國的國際度量衡局彙整。

cards.body_en: Taiwan's official time today is called National Standard Time, UTC+8. It is kept by atomic clocks at Chunghwa Telecom Laboratories on behalf of the Bureau of Standards, and dialing 117 plays it. But it has changed. According to the Taiwan Historica archive, from October 1, 1937 to September 21, 1945 Taiwan used Japan's time, one hour ahead. From 1946 Taiwan used summer time in many years, and it stopped in the early 1980s.
cards.body_zh: 台灣現行的標準時間叫做「國家標準時間」，是 UTC+8，由經濟部標準檢驗局委託中華電信研究院用原子鐘維護；撥 117 聽到的報時就是它。但它改過。依國史館臺灣文獻館的文章，1937 年 10 月 1 日到 1945 年 9 月 21 日，台灣用的是快一小時的日本中央標準時間；1946 年起許多年份實施「夏令時間」，到 1980 年代初期停止。

cards.body_en: Because each country chooses its own date, the date line can move. At midnight on December 29, 2011, Samoa and Tokelau moved from the eastern side of the date line to the western side, to keep business hours closer to their trading partners in Asia and Oceania. For them, December 30, 2011 never happened.
cards.body_zh: 因為每個國家自己決定日期，換日線是會移動的。2011 年 12 月 29 日午夜，薩摩亞和托克勞從換日線的東邊換到西邊，好讓營業時間和亞洲、大洋洲的貿易夥伴更接近。對他們來說，2011 年 12 月 30 日根本沒有出現。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum (2018). The words time zone and date line do not appear in it. Day and night belong to natural science, and longitude to junior high geography; the links below are our reading of them.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要（民國 107 年發布）。課綱裡沒有出現「時區」和「換日線」；晝夜屬於自然科學，經緯度屬於國中地理。下面和本課的連結是本教材的解讀。

items.text: 夏季白天較長，冬季黑夜較長。
items.note_en: The explanation for this entry says: “說明地球自轉會造成晝夜交替現象。” (Explain that the Earth's rotation causes day and night.) The 3D model shows exactly that, and the season buttons show the changing day length.
items.note_zh: 這一條的學習內容說明寫：「說明地球自轉會造成晝夜交替現象。」3D 模型示範的就是這件事，季節按鈕則讓你看到白天的長短改變。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 日出日落時間與位置，在不同季節會不同。
items.note_en: Sunrise and sunset happen where a place crosses the line between day and night.
items.note_zh: 日出、日落，就是一個地方跨過晝夜交界的那一刻。

items.text: 全球經緯度座標系統。
items.note_en: Idealized time zones are counted in steps of 15 degrees of longitude.
items.note_zh: 理想時區就是用經度每 15 度一格來算的。

myths.myth_en: The Sun travels around the Earth once a day.
myths.myth_zh: 太陽每天繞著地球跑一圈。
myths.fact_en: The Earth spins toward the east, so the Sun only seems to cross the sky from east to west.
myths.fact_zh: 是地球往東自轉，太陽才看起來從東往西走過天空。

myths.myth_en: Time zones are straight strips, each exactly 15 degrees wide.
myths.myth_zh: 時區是一條一條筆直的帶子，每條剛好 15 度寬。
myths.fact_en: That is only the idealized picture. Real time zone boundaries bend to follow the borders of countries and regions, and some places use half hours.
myths.fact_zh: 那只是理想的畫法。真實的時區界線會跟著國家和地區的邊界彎曲，有些地方還用半小時。

myths.myth_en: An international treaty fixed the International Date Line.
myths.myth_zh: 國際換日線是國際條約規定的。
myths.fact_en: According to NOAA, the date line has no legal international status; each country chooses the date it uses. That is why the line zigzags.
myths.fact_zh: 依美國國家海洋暨大氣總署的說明，換日線沒有國際法律地位，每個國家自己決定用哪一天的日期，所以這條線彎彎曲曲。

myths.myth_en: Exactly half of the Earth is in daylight at every moment.
myths.myth_zh: 任何時候，地球都剛好一半是白天。
myths.fact_en: Slightly more than half is lit, because the atmosphere bends sunlight around the edge. That is also why the line between day and night is fuzzy, not sharp.
myths.fact_zh: 被照亮的部分比一半多一點，因為大氣會把陽光折到邊緣後面。所以晝夜的交界是模糊的，不是一條清楚的線。

tricks.body_en: 360 degrees in 24 hours means 15 degrees every hour.
tricks.body_zh: 24 小時轉 360 度，每小時 15 度。

tricks.body_en: The Sun reaches the east first, so places to the east are later in the day.
tricks.body_zh: 太陽先照到東邊，所以東邊的地方時間比較晚、鐘比較快。

tricks.title_en: West over the line, add a day
tricks.body_en: Cross the date line going west and the date jumps forward; going east, it goes back.
tricks.body_zh: 往西跨過換日線，日期往前跳；往東跨過，日期退回。

tricks.body_en: Find the zone, count the hours, and watch for midnight.
tricks.body_zh: 找時區、算小時、注意半夜。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Never look straight at the Sun, and never look at it through a lens or a phone camera.
safety.zh: 絕對不要直視太陽，也不要透過鏡片或手機鏡頭看太陽。

safety.en: If you use a lamp as the Sun, keep your hands and paper away from the hot bulb, and let an adult plug it in.
safety.zh: 如果用檯燈當太陽，手和紙張不要碰到燙的燈泡，插電交給大人。

safety.en: When you mark shadows outside, stay in the playground where your teacher can see you, and wear a hat in strong sun.
safety.zh: 到戶外記錄影子時，待在老師看得到的操場，太陽大時戴帽子。

safety.en: Use a pushpin only with an adult's help, and press it into the ball away from your fingers.
safety.zh: 圖釘要在大人幫忙下使用，壓進球裡時手指要避開。

activities.title_en: Day and Night with a Lamp

materials.en: A desk lamp (the Sun)
A globe or a ball with a line drawn around the middle
materials.zh: 一顆地球儀，或畫了赤道的球

materials.en: Two small stickers, one for Taipei and one for New York
materials.zh: 兩張小貼紙，一張是台北、一張是紐約

materials.en: A dark room

steps.en: Put the stickers on the globe: Taipei near 25 degrees north, 121 degrees east; New York near 41 degrees north, 74 degrees west.
steps.zh: 把貼紙貼在地球儀上：台北大約在北緯 25 度、東經 121 度；紐約大約在北緯 41 度、西經 74 度。

steps.en: Turn on the lamp and point it at the globe. Which half is day? Which half is night?
steps.zh: 打開檯燈照著地球儀。哪一半是白天？哪一半是黑夜？

steps.en: Turn the globe slowly from west to east, counterclockwise when you look down on the North Pole.
steps.zh: 慢慢把地球儀由西向東轉，從北極往下看是逆時針。

steps.en: Stop when Taipei faces the lamp. Where is New York? Keep turning until New York faces the lamp.
steps.zh: 轉到台北正對著檯燈時停下來。紐約在哪裡？繼續轉，直到紐約正對著檯燈。

steps.en: Count how much of a turn that took. About half a turn means about half a day apart.
steps.zh: 數一數轉了多少。大約半圈，就表示兩地大約差半天。

activities.tip_en: Turning the globe, not moving the lamp, is the key idea: the Sun does not race around the Earth; the Earth turns.
activities.tip_zh: 重點是轉地球儀、不是移動檯燈：不是太陽繞著地球跑，是地球自己在轉。

activities.title_en: A World Clock for the Classroom

materials.en: Paper plates, one for each city
Paper hands and brass fasteners
A world map without borders, or the one in this lesson
materials.zh: 一張沒有國界的世界地圖，或本課的地圖

steps.en: Choose five cities and find their longitudes. Divide each by 15 and round to get its idealized time zone.
steps.zh: 選五個城市，查出經度。每個經度除以 15 再四捨五入，就是理想時區。

steps.en: Make a clock from each plate and write the city and its time zone, such as “Taipei, UTC+8,” under it.
steps.zh: 用紙盤做時鐘，在下面寫上城市和時區，例如「台北 UTC+8」。

steps.en: Set the Taipei clock to the time now. Work out each of the other clocks and set them.
steps.zh: 把台北的鐘撥到現在的時間，再算出其他每個鐘，撥好。

steps.en: Hang the clocks in order from west to east, the same order as on the map.
steps.zh: 照地圖上由西到東的順序，把鐘掛起來。

steps.en: Check a real world clock online. Which ones are different, and why? Look for daylight saving time or half-hour zones.
steps.zh: 對照網路上真正的世界時間。哪幾個不一樣？為什麼？找找看是不是夏令時間或半小時的時區。

activities.tip_en: Idealized zones are a starting point. Real time zones follow decisions made by each country, so always check before an important call or flight.
activities.tip_zh: 理想時區只是起點。真實的時區是各地自己決定的，重要的電話或班機之前一定要查清楚。

links_head.zh: 其他課裡的時間，以及下一課

links.zh: 怎麼找到地球上任何一個地方？
links.note_en: Longitude, the prime meridian, and the clock that solved the longitude problem.
links.note_zh: 經度、本初子午線，以及解決經度難題的那座鐘。

links.en: Why Do We Have Seasons?
links.zh: 為什麼有四季？
links.note_en: Why the line between day and night tilts with the seasons.
links.note_zh: 晝夜的交界為什麼會隨季節傾斜。

links.en: Why Does the Sun Rise in a Different Place Every Day?
links.zh: 太陽為什麼每天從不同的地方升起？
links.note_en: Sunrise from the ground, on the same turning Earth.
links.note_zh: 在同一顆轉動的地球上，從地面看日出。

links.zh: 世界有幾大洲、幾大洋？

links.note_zh: 怎麼把世界分成大洲和大洋，以及為什麼不只一種算法。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). Clock times, day and night, and the answers to the game are computed by the page itself and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；時間、晝夜與小遊戲的答案都由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試

sources.en: “Earth rotates from west to east, so the sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west.”
sources.zh: 地球由西向東自轉，所以太陽看起來東升西落
sources.src: National Geographic Education, “Earth”

sources.en: “Within the 360° daily rotation of the Earth, the sun moves 15° each hour, which leads to the formation of 24 time zones”; zone boundaries “are no longer straight, nor are they always continuous.”
sources.zh: 地球一天轉 360 度、每小時 15 度，形成 24 個時區；時區界線不再是直線
sources.src: NOAA JetStream, “Z-time”

sources.en: A time zone is “one of Earth's 24 divisions distinct by one hour, roughly 15 degrees of longitude”; many places use half-hour time zones.
sources.zh: 時區是地球的 24 個區之一、相差一小時、大約 15 度經度；有些地方用半小時的時區
sources.src: National Geographic Education, “MapMaker: World Time Zones”

sources.en: UTC is “the modern equivalent of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is never more than half a second different from it.”
sources.zh: 協調世界時是格林威治標準時間的現代版本，相差不超過半秒
sources.src: Royal Museums Greenwich, “Which time is it?”

sources.en: International Atomic Time is computed by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM); UTC is based on it.
sources.zh: 國際原子時由國際度量衡局計算，協調世界時以它為基礎
sources.src: NIST, “How UTC(NIST) is related to Coordinated Universal Time”

sources.en: On November 18, 1883, railroad station clocks were reset as standard-time noon was reached in each time zone: the Day of Two Noons.
sources.zh: 1883 年 11 月 18 日，各時區到了標準時間的正午就重設車站的鐘，稱為兩個正午的一天
sources.src: Library of Congress, “The Day of Two Noons”

sources.en: U.S. Eastern Time: EST is UTC−5 and EDT is UTC−4; daylight saving time begins on the second Sunday of March and ends on the first Sunday of November.
sources.zh: 美國東部時間：標準時間 UTC−5、夏令時間 UTC−4；夏令時間從三月第二個星期日到十一月第一個星期日
sources.src: NIST, “Local Time FAQs” and “Daylight Saving Time”

sources.en: “The international date line has no legal international status and countries are free to choose the dates that they observe”; it zigzags around political borders.
sources.zh: 國際換日線沒有國際法律地位，各國自己選擇日期；它會繞著政治邊界彎曲
sources.src: NOAA National Ocean Service, “What is the international date line?”

sources.en: The line between day and night is called the terminator; because the atmosphere bends sunlight, the sunlit area is greater than the dark area.
sources.zh: 晝夜的交界叫晨昏線；大氣折射陽光，所以照到陽光的面積比黑暗的大
sources.src: NOAA Science On a Sphere, “Day/Night Terminator”

sources.en: Samoa and Tokelau moved to the western side of the date line at midnight on December 29, 2011, “thus losing December 30th.”
sources.zh: 2011 年 12 月 29 日午夜，薩摩亞與托克勞移到換日線西側，少了 12 月 30 日
sources.src: U.S. Department of State, Geographer's Guidance Bulletin No. 31 (2012)

sources.en: Taiwan's current standard time is called National Standard Time, UTC+8; the term 中原標準時間 is no longer used; the 117 time service comes from atomic clocks.
sources.zh: 「臺灣現行採用的標準時間，稱為「國家標準時間」，比世界協調時快8小時，即UTC+8。」「中原標準時間」現今已不再使用；117 報時來自原子鐘
sources.src: 國立科學工藝博物館・中華電信〈電信文物：報時〉

sources.en: Taiwan's national time and frequency standard is maintained by Chunghwa Telecom Laboratories on behalf of the Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection.
sources.zh: 「臺灣的國家標準時頻由本局委託中華電信研究院維護」
sources.src: 經濟部標準檢驗局

sources.en: Taiwan used Japan's Central Standard Time from October 1, 1937 to September 21, 1945; summer time from 1946, stopped in the early 1980s.
sources.zh: 1937 年 10 月 1 日起改用日本中央標準時間，1945 年 9 月 21 日恢復；1946 年起實施夏令時間，1980 年代初期停止
sources.src: 國史館臺灣文獻館 電子報

sources.en: Chinese terms: 時區, 標準時, 地方時, 太陽時, 協調世界時, 格林威治標準時間, 國際換日線, 日光節約時間, 晨昏線, 自轉.
sources.zh: 中文名詞依國家教育研究院樂詞網（地理學名詞、高中以下地理學名詞、天文學名詞、氣象學名詞）
sources.src: 國家教育研究院 樂詞網

sources.en: Curriculum entries 自 Id-Ⅳ-1 and its explanation, 自 INc-Ⅲ-13 (natural science), 地 Aa-Ⅳ-1 (social studies).
sources.zh: 課綱條目 自 Id-Ⅳ-1（含學習內容說明）、自 INc-Ⅲ-13（自然科學領域）、地 Aa-Ⅳ-1（社會領域）

lessons.title: How Many Continents and Oceans Are There?
lessons.blurb_en: Color the land of a 3D Earth by continent and the sea by ocean, then switch between different ways of counting them. See why the answer can be seven, six, or five continents, and four or five oceans.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球上，把陸地依大洲上色、海洋依大洋上色，再切換不同的算法。看看為什麼答案可以是七、六或五大洲，四或五大洋。
lessons.big_idea_en: Where the land and the water are is a fact of geography. How we divide them into continents and oceans, and what we call each part, is something people agree on. That is why there is more than one way to count.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 陸地和海水在哪裡，是地理的事實；怎麼把它們分成大洲、大洋，每一塊叫什麼名字，是人約定的。所以算法不只一種。

lab.title_en: One World, Many Ways to Count
lab.title_zh: 同一個世界，不同的算法
lab.how_en: The land is colored by continent. Choose a way to count the continents and watch the colors regroup. Turn on the oceans to color the sea, with four or five oceans. Tap any land or sea to see which group it belongs to. Only colors are used; no borders are drawn, and the lines between continents follow common conventions, not lines on the ground.
lab.how_zh: 陸地依大洲上色。選一種大洲的算法，看顏色怎麼重新分組。打開大洋，海也會上色，可以選四大洋或五大洋。點任何一塊陸地或海，看它屬於哪一組。這裡只用顏色，不畫國界；大洲之間的分界照常見的約定，不是地上真的有一條線。
lab.scale_en: The lines between continents and oceans are drawn by rules of thumb that follow common conventions (for example, the Ural Mountains, the Suez Isthmus, the Panama Isthmus, and 60 degrees south for the Southern Ocean). Other sources draw some of them a little differently.
lab.scale_zh: 大洲、大洋之間的分界是照常見約定的簡化規則畫的（例如烏拉山、蘇伊士地峽、巴拿馬地峽、南大洋以南緯 60 度為界）。其他資料有些地方畫得不太一樣。
lab.credit_html: Land outlines: Natural Earth, 1:50m Land, version 5.1.2, public domain. The grouping into continents and oceans is our own, by longitude and latitude, following common conventions. Areas shown when you tap come from the sources listed at the bottom of the page. · 陸地外形：Natural Earth 1:50m Land 5.1.2 版，公有領域。大洲、大洋的分組是本教材依經緯度、照常見約定自己分的；點選時顯示的面積出自頁尾的資料來源。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four ways to look at the world

parts.text_en: Seven colors for seven continents. Notice that Europe and Asia touch along a long stretch of land, and Africa almost touches Asia.
parts.text_zh: 七種顏色代表七大洲。注意歐洲和亞洲有一長段陸地是連在一起的，非洲也幾乎和亞洲相連。

parts.text_en: Join Europe and Asia into Eurasia and the count drops to six. The land did not move; only the way we group it changed.
parts.text_zh: 把歐洲和亞洲合成歐亞大陸，就剩六個。陸地沒有移動，改變的只是分組的方式。

parts.text_en: Join Europe and Asia, and also North and South America. Eurasia, America, Africa, Antarctica, and Australia make five.
parts.text_zh: 歐亞合一，南北美也合一：歐亞大陸、美洲、非洲、南極洲、澳洲，一共五個。

parts.text_en: Color the oceans and switch between four and five. With five, the water around Antarctica becomes the Southern Ocean.
parts.text_zh: 把大洋上色，在四大洋和五大洋之間切換。選五大洋時，南極洲周圍的海就成了南大洋。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Tap the land near the Red Sea, near Panama, and near the Ural Mountains. Which places change group when you change the way of counting?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。點紅海附近、巴拿馬附近、烏拉山附近的陸地。換一種算法時，哪些地方會換組？

bars.lead_en: The bars show the areas of the continents and the oceans. Tap one to see how many Taiwans would fit inside it.
bars.lead_zh: 長條是各大洲、各大洋的面積。點一條，看裡面大約放得下幾個台灣。
bars.note_en: Areas: Encyclopaedia Britannica (continents read October 2026); Australia and Oceania from the Wikipedia “Continent” table, which adds up Britannica's figures. Britannica measures some oceans without their smaller nearby seas (the Pacific without the South China Sea, the Atlantic and the Indian Ocean without their marginal seas), so other sources give larger numbers. Taiwan: 35,887 square kilometers for the main island and 21 smaller islands (Executive Yuan).
bars.note_zh: 面積：大英百科全書（2026 年 10 月查閱）；澳洲與大洋洲取自維基百科「Continent」條目的表格（加總大英百科的數字）。大英百科有些大洋不含旁邊較小的海（太平洋不含南海，大西洋、印度洋不含邊緣海），所以其他資料的數字會比較大。台灣：本島及 21 個附屬島嶼共 35,887 平方公里（行政院）。

count.lead_en: Eight questions. Each one first tells you the way of counting, then asks how many there are or where a place belongs. Every way of counting is used somewhere in the world, so the question is always “by this count.” There is no timer, and the game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
count.lead_zh: 八道題。每一題先告訴你用哪一種算法，再問有幾個，或某個地方屬於哪一組。每一種算法世界上都有人用，所以問的永遠是「照這種算法」。不計時，遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。
count.hint_en: Read the rule again. Which groups does it join together, and which does it leave out?
count.hint_zh: 再讀一次規則：它把哪些合在一起？又把哪些拿掉？
count.start_en: Use only the rule shown above. There is no single “real” answer.
count.start_zh: 只照上面的規則來想，沒有唯一「真正」的答案。
count.end_en: Next time someone asks how many continents there are, you can ask back: “How are you counting?”
count.end_zh: 下次有人問世界有幾大洲，你可以反問：「你怎麼算？」

questions.rule_en: Rule: Europe and Asia are one continent, Eurasia. Every other continent stays on its own.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：歐洲和亞洲算同一洲（歐亞大陸），其他各洲照舊分開。
questions.en: By this rule, how many continents are there?
questions.zh: 照這個規則，有幾大洲？
questions.why_en: Seven continents minus one, because two of them became one: six.
questions.why_zh: 七大洲裡有兩個合成一個，所以是六個。

questions.rule_en: Rule: Europe and Asia are one continent, and North and South America are one continent too.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：歐洲和亞洲算一洲，南北美洲也算一洲。
questions.en: By this rule, how many continents are there?
questions.zh: 照這個規則，有幾大洲？
questions.why_en: Two pairs become two continents, so seven drops to five: Eurasia, America, Africa, Antarctica, and Australia.
questions.why_zh: 兩對各合成一個，七個就變成五個：歐亞大陸、美洲、非洲、南極洲、澳洲。

questions.rule_en: Rule: Europe and Asia are one continent, Eurasia.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：歐洲和亞洲算同一洲（歐亞大陸）。
questions.en: The island marked on the map is Iceland. By this rule, which continent is it part of?
questions.zh: 地圖上標的島是冰島。照這個規則，它屬於哪一洲？
questions.why_en: In the usual seven-continent count, Iceland is part of Europe, and by this rule Europe is part of Eurasia.
questions.why_zh: 在常見的七大洲算法裡，冰島算在歐洲，而照這個規則，歐洲是歐亞大陸的一部分。

questions.rule_en: Rule: North and South America are one continent, America. Europe and Asia stay separate.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：南北美洲算同一洲（美洲），歐洲和亞洲照舊分開。
questions.en: The big island marked on the map is Greenland. By this rule, which continent is it part of?
questions.zh: 地圖上標的大島是格陵蘭。照這個規則，它屬於哪一洲？
questions.why_en: In the usual seven-continent count, Greenland is part of North America, and by this rule North America is part of America.
questions.why_zh: 在常見的七大洲算法裡，格陵蘭算在北美洲，而照這個規則，北美洲是美洲的一部分。

questions.en: The island marked on the map is Madagascar. Which continent is it counted with?
questions.zh: 地圖上標的島是馬達加斯加。它算在哪一洲？
questions.why_en: Islands are usually counted with the nearest continent. Madagascar lies just off the coast of Africa.
questions.why_zh: 島嶼通常算在離它最近的大洲。馬達加斯加就在非洲的外海。

questions.rule_en: Rule: the usual seven continents, with North and South America meeting at the Isthmus of Panama.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：常見的七大洲，南北美洲在巴拿馬地峽相接。
questions.en: The point on the map is on the narrow land just west of where North and South America meet. Which continent is it in?
questions.zh: 地圖上的點在南北美洲交界處稍微偏西的狹長陸地上。它在哪一洲？
questions.why_en: The usual line is drawn near the border between Panama and Colombia, so the narrow land of Panama is counted with North America.
questions.why_zh: 常見的分界畫在巴拿馬和哥倫比亞交界附近，所以巴拿馬那段狹長的陸地算在北美洲。

questions.rule_en: Rule: five oceans. The Southern Ocean is the water around Antarctica, south of 60 degrees south.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：五大洋。南大洋是南極洲周圍、南緯 60 度以南的海。
questions.en: Which ocean is the point marked on the map in?
questions.zh: 地圖上標的點在哪一個大洋？
questions.why_en: The point is at 65 degrees south, south of 60 degrees south, so by this rule it is in the Southern Ocean.
questions.why_zh: 這個點在南緯 65 度，在南緯 60 度以南，所以照這個規則屬於南大洋。

questions.rule_en: Rule: four oceans, with no Southern Ocean. The water around Antarctica belongs to the ocean to its north.
questions.rule_zh: 規則：四大洋，沒有南大洋。南極洲周圍的海算在它北邊的那個大洋。
questions.en: It is the same point as before. Which ocean is it in now?
questions.zh: 還是同一個點。現在它在哪一個大洋？
questions.why_en: Without a Southern Ocean, the water south of New Zealand and Australia's east coast counts as part of the Pacific Ocean.
questions.why_zh: 沒有南大洋時，紐西蘭與澳洲東岸以南的海就算在太平洋。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about continents and oceans
map_english.zh: 談大洲與大洋的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about the big pieces of the world. Listen, repeat, then use them to describe where a place is.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說世界的大塊陸地與大片海洋。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用這些句子描述一個地方在哪裡。

items.en: Asia is the largest continent on Earth.
items.zh: 亞洲是地球上最大的洲。

items.en: The Pacific is the largest ocean, and the deepest too.
items.zh: 太平洋是最大的大洋，也是最深的。

items.en: Taiwan is in Asia, on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.
items.zh: 台灣在亞洲，位在太平洋的邊緣。
items.use_en: is in …, on the edge of …

items.en: The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica.
items.zh: 南大洋環繞著南極洲。

items.en: Europe and Asia are part of the same landmass.
items.zh: 歐洲和亞洲是同一塊大陸的一部分。

items.en: Some people count seven continents, and others count six.
items.zh: 有些人算七大洲，也有人算六大洲。

items.en: The Isthmus of Panama connects North America and South America.
items.zh: 巴拿馬地峽連接北美洲和南美洲。

items.en: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
items.zh: 非洲和澳洲之間是哪一個大洋？

tricks_head.en: Continents and oceans in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住大洲與大洋

tricks.body_en: Seven, six, and five are all in use. Ask which way someone is counting.
tricks.body_zh: 七、六、五都有人用；先問對方用哪一種算法。

tricks.body_en: Africa meets Asia at Suez, and North America meets South America at Panama.
tricks.body_zh: 非洲和亞洲在蘇伊士相連，北美和南美在巴拿馬相連。

tricks.body_en: All the oceans are connected; their names divide one world ocean.
tricks.body_zh: 各大洋其實是連在一起的；名字只是把一個世界海洋分開來叫。

tricks.title_zh: 南緯 60 以南是南大洋
tricks.body_en: When five oceans are counted, the Southern Ocean is the water around Antarctica.
tricks.body_zh: 算五大洋的時候，南極洲周圍的海就是南大洋。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Use scissors carefully. Cut away from your body, and pass them to others with the handles first.
safety.zh: 小心使用剪刀，往身體外側剪；遞給別人時握把朝向對方。

safety.en: Toss the inflatable globe gently and underhand, only to a partner who is ready, and keep the area clear.
safety.zh: 充氣地球儀要輕輕地由下往上拋，只拋給準備好的同伴，周圍保持淨空。

safety.en: Do not throw the globe near windows, lights, or people who are not playing.
safety.zh: 不要在窗戶、燈具或沒有參加的人附近丟球。

safety.en: Blow up the globe with a pump if you have one. If you feel dizzy while blowing, stop and rest.
safety.zh: 有打氣筒就用打氣筒充氣；自己吹氣時覺得頭暈，就停下來休息。

materials.en: A printed world map with no borders, such as one made from the 3D model's flat view or a blank outline map
materials.zh: 一張沒有國界的世界地圖，例如空白輪廓圖

materials.en: Scissors and glue
Three large sheets of paper

steps.en: Cut out the big pieces of land. Where land is connected, keep it in one piece.
steps.zh: 把大塊的陸地剪下來。陸地連在一起的地方，就保持一整塊。

steps.en: Count your pieces. Is the number seven? Which continents stayed joined together?
steps.zh: 數一數有幾塊。是七塊嗎？哪些大洲還連在一起？

steps.en: On the first sheet, group the pieces into seven continents. You will need to cut where people usually draw the lines.
steps.zh: 在第一張紙上分成七大洲。你需要在大家通常畫線的地方剪開。

steps.en: On the second sheet, group them into six. On the third, group them into five.
steps.zh: 在第二張紙上分成六大洲；第三張分成五大洲。

steps.en: Compare the three sheets. Write one sentence about what changed and what stayed the same.
steps.zh: 比較三張紙，寫一句話：什麼改變了？什麼沒有變？

activities.tip_en: The land is the same on all three sheets. Only the grouping changes. That is the big idea of this lesson.
activities.tip_zh: 三張紙上的陸地都一樣，改變的只有分組。這就是這一課的核心概念。

activities.title_en: Catch the Globe: How Much Is Water?

materials.en: An inflatable globe or a beach ball with a world map
materials.zh: 一顆充氣地球儀，或印有世界地圖的海灘球

materials.en: A tally sheet with two columns: land and water
materials.zh: 一張記錄表，分成「陸地」和「水」兩欄

steps.en: Stand in a circle. Toss the globe gently to a classmate.
steps.zh: 圍成一圈，把地球儀輕輕拋給一位同學。

steps.en: The catcher looks at where their right thumb landed: land or water? Make a tally mark.
steps.zh: 接住的人看右手大拇指落在哪裡：陸地還是水？在記錄表上畫一筆。

steps.en: Keep going until you have at least 50 catches.
steps.zh: 一直玩到至少接了 50 次。

steps.en: Divide the number of water catches by the total. What fraction of your catches landed on water?
steps.zh: 用落在水上的次數除以總次數。你們有幾成落在水上？

steps.en: Compare your answer with the number on this page. The more catches you make, the closer you usually get.
steps.zh: 把你們的答案和本頁的數字比一比。接得越多次，通常就越接近。

activities.tip_en: This is called sampling: many random tries give a good estimate of the whole.
activities.tip_zh: 這叫做「抽樣」：隨機試很多次，就能大致估計整體。

links.zh: 各大洲是什麼樣子？

links.note_zh: 單元六一洲一洲去看亞洲、歐洲、非洲、北美洲、南美洲與大洋洲。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026). The grouping of land and sea, the land-or-water check, and the answers to the game are computed by the page itself and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；陸地與海的分組、點選時的判斷和小遊戲的答案都由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試
paras: Ask a class how many continents there are, and you may hear more than one answer. Many students say seven. Some say six, and a few say five. Here is the surprise: each of these answers is taught somewhere in the world. Which one is right depends on how you count.

A continent is one of the main divisions of land on Earth. But look at a globe, and you will see that the land does not come in neat, separate pieces. Europe and Asia sit on one huge piece of land. Africa is joined to Asia by the narrow Isthmus of Suez, and South America is joined to North America by the narrow Isthmus of Panama. The lines between continents were drawn by people, not by nature. National Geographic calls the line between Europe and Asia an imaginary one.

So there is more than one way to count. By convention, many people count seven continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia. Some geographers join Europe and Asia into Eurasia, which gives six. In some countries, students learn that North and South America are one continent, America, which also gives six. Join both pairs, and you get five: Eurasia, America, Africa, Antarctica, and Australia.

The oceans are counted in different ways too. The U.S. National Ocean Service puts it simply: “There is only one global ocean.” All the water is connected, and the names divide it into parts. For a long time, people named four oceans: the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Indian, and the Arctic. Today most countries also count a fifth, the Southern Ocean, which surrounds Antarctica from its coast to 60 degrees south. National Geographic began counting it in 2021, and in 2023 the International Hydrographic Organization approved a resolution recognizing it.

Whichever way you count, some facts stay the same. About 71 percent of Earth's surface is covered by ocean. Asia is the largest continent, with about 44.6 million square kilometers. The Pacific is the largest ocean: even without the South China Sea, it covers about 161.8 million square kilometers, more than all the land on Earth put together.

And Taiwan? In the seven-continent count, Taiwan is in Asia. Taiwan's Executive Yuan describes the island as lying in the middle of the East Asian island arc, with the Pacific Ocean to its east. Its main island and 21 smaller islands cover about 35,887 square kilometers, so Asia could hold more than 1,200 Taiwans. The next time someone asks how many continents there are, you can answer with a question: “How are you counting?”
paras_zh: 問全班世界有幾大洲，你可能會聽到不只一個答案。很多同學說七個，有人說六個，還有人說五個。令人驚訝的是：這些答案世界上都有地方在教。哪一個對，要看你怎麼算。
大洲是地球上陸地的主要分區。可是看看地球儀，你會發現陸地並不是一塊一塊整齊分開的。歐洲和亞洲在同一大塊陸地上。非洲靠著狹窄的蘇伊士地峽和亞洲相連，南美洲靠著狹窄的巴拿馬地峽和北美洲相連。大洲之間的界線是人畫的，不是大自然畫的。國家地理學會就說，歐洲和亞洲之間的那條線是想像出來的。
所以算法不只一種。照慣例，很多人算七大洲：亞洲、非洲、北美洲、南美洲、南極洲、歐洲、澳洲。有些地理學家把歐洲和亞洲合成歐亞大陸，就是六個。有些國家的學生學到南北美洲是同一洲（美洲），也是六個。兩對都合起來，就是五個：歐亞大陸、美洲、非洲、南極洲、澳洲。
大洋也有不同的算法。美國國家海洋局說得很簡單：「全世界只有一個海洋。」所有的海水都是相連的，名字只是把它分成幾個部分。很長一段時間，人們只命名了四個大洋：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋和北冰洋（也叫北極海）。現在大多數國家還算第五個：南大洋，也就是從南極洲海岸到南緯 60 度、環繞南極洲的海。國家地理學會從 2021 年開始算它，2023 年國際水文組織也通過了承認它的決議。
不管怎麼算，有些事實不會變。地球表面大約 71% 被海洋覆蓋。亞洲是最大的洲，大約 4,460 萬平方公里。太平洋是最大的大洋：就算不算南海，也有大約 1 億 6,180 萬平方公里，比地球上所有的陸地加起來還大。
那台灣呢？在七大洲的算法裡，台灣在亞洲。行政院的介紹說，台灣位在東亞島弧的中央，東邊面臨太平洋。台灣本島和 21 個附屬島嶼合起來大約 35,887 平方公里，所以亞洲放得下一千二百多個台灣。下次有人問世界有幾大洲，你可以用一個問題回答：「你怎麼算？」
questions: Why can people give different answers to “How many continents are there?” and all be right?
Which two narrow pieces of land join continents together, and which continents do they join?
Why do people say there is really only one global ocean?
answers: Because the lines between continents are drawn by people. Some counts join Europe and Asia, or North and South America, so the number can be seven, six, or five.
The Isthmus of Suez joins Africa and Asia, and the Isthmus of Panama joins North America and South America.
All the oceans are connected, so the water flows from one to another. The names divide one ocean into parts.
