myths.myth_en: Everyone in the world agrees there are seven continents.
myths.myth_zh: 全世界都同意有七大洲。
myths.fact_en: Seven is common, but six and five are also taught. The number depends on which pieces of land are grouped together.
myths.fact_zh: 七大洲很常見，但也有人教六大洲、五大洲；數目要看哪些陸地被合在一起。

myths.myth_en: Europe and Asia are separated by the sea.
myths.myth_zh: 歐洲和亞洲之間隔著海。
myths.fact_en: They are one landmass. The usual line runs along the Ural Mountains and the Caspian and Black Seas, and it was drawn by people.
myths.fact_zh: 它們是同一塊大陸。常見的分界沿著烏拉山、裏海和黑海，是人畫出來的。

myths.myth_en: Each ocean is a separate body of water.
myths.myth_zh: 每一個大洋都是分開的一片水。
myths.fact_en: All the oceans are connected. There is one global ocean, and the names divide it into parts.
myths.fact_zh: 所有的大洋都是相連的。全世界只有一個海洋，名字只是把它分成幾個部分。

myths.myth_en: The Southern Ocean is brand-new water.
myths.myth_zh: 南大洋是新出現的海。
myths.fact_en: The water was always there. What changed is the naming: the IHO used the name in 1937, dropped it in 1953, and approved a resolution recognizing it in 2023.
myths.fact_zh: 那片海一直都在，改變的是命名：國際水文組織 1937 年用過這個名字，1953 年拿掉，2023 年又通過決議承認它。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Names · 名字背後的故事
culture_cards.lead_en: There is no single office that decides how many continents there are. Here are four moments when people counted the world in different ways.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 世界上沒有一個機關決定有幾大洲。下面是四個人們用不同方式數世界的時刻。

cards.k: Olympic Charter · 奧林匹克憲章
cards.body_en: The Olympic Charter says the five interlocking rings represent “the union of the five continents and the meeting of athletes from throughout the world.” The charter does not say which five continents it means.
cards.body_zh: 《奧林匹克憲章》說，五個相扣的環代表「五大洲的團結，以及全世界運動員的相聚」。憲章並沒有說是哪五個洲。

cards.k: 2021 · National Geographic · 國家地理學會
cards.en: A fifth ocean on the map
cards.body_en: National Geographic had recognized four oceans since it began making maps in 1915. On June 8, 2021, World Oceans Day, it began recognizing the Southern Ocean as the fifth. The U.S. Board on Geographic Names had already been using the name since 1999.
cards.body_zh: 國家地理學會從 1915 年開始製作地圖，一直只承認四個大洋。2021 年 6 月 8 日世界海洋日，它開始把南大洋算作第五個。美國地名委員會則從 1999 年起就已經使用這個名字。

cards.body_en: The International Hydrographic Organization publishes the limits of oceans and seas. In May 2023 its Assembly approved a resolution recognizing the Southern Ocean, with its northern limit at 60 degrees south. Argentina asked for its own position to be attached to the record.
cards.body_zh: 國際水文組織出版海洋與海的界限。2023 年 5 月，它的大會通過決議承認南大洋，北界定在南緯 60 度。阿根廷要求把自己的立場附在紀錄上。

cards.body_en: In 2017, geologists described a 4.9-million-square-kilometer region of continental crust in the southwest Pacific, around New Zealand, and called it Zealandia. About 94 percent of it is under water. Not everyone agrees it should count as a continent.
cards.body_zh: 2017 年，地質學家描述了西南太平洋、紐西蘭周圍一片 490 萬平方公里的大陸地殼，稱它為「西蘭大陸」。它大約 94% 在海面下。不是每個人都同意它應該算一個洲。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (2018). The curriculum does not say how many continents there are; the words seven, six, or five continents do not appear in it. The links below are our reading.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年發布）。課綱沒有規定有幾大洲，裡面也沒有出現「七大洲」「六大洲」「五大洲」。下面和本課的連結是本教材的解讀。

items.text: 全球海陸分布。
items.note_en: This lesson is about exactly this: where the land and the water are, and how people group them.
items.note_zh: 這一課講的正是這件事：陸地和海在哪裡，人們又怎麼把它們分組。

items.text: 臺灣地理位置的特性及其影響。
items.note_en: Taiwan sits between the largest continent and the largest ocean.
items.note_zh: 台灣就位在最大的洲和最大的大洋之間。

items.area: 社會領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 臺灣的地理位置、自然環境，與歷史文化的發展有關聯性。
items.note_en: Finding Taiwan on the globe, next to Asia and the Pacific, is the first step.
items.note_zh: 在地球儀上找到台灣、看見它旁邊的亞洲與太平洋，是第一步。

sources.en: A continent is “one of Earth's seven main divisions of land”; the line between Europe and Asia is “an imaginary line”; Africa is joined to Asia by the Isthmus of Suez, and South America to North America by the Isthmus of Panama; the continents add up to about 148 million square kilometers.
sources.zh: 大洲是地球七大陸地分區之一；歐亞之間是一條想像的線；蘇伊士地峽、巴拿馬地峽；陸地約 1 億 4,800 萬平方公里
sources.src: National Geographic Education, “Continent”

sources.en: “By convention there are seven continents”; “Some geographers list only six continents, combining Europe and Asia into Eurasia”; some students learn five: “Eurasia, Australia, Africa, Antarctica, and the Americas.”
sources.zh: 七大洲是慣例；有些地理學家只列六個（歐亞合一）；也有人學五個
sources.src: National Geographic, Geography FAQ (archived 2008)

sources.en: The six-continent count with North and South America as one continent is taught in some countries.
sources.zh: 有些國家教南北美合一的六大洲
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Continent”

sources.en: “There is only one global ocean”; “Historically, there are four named oceans: the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, and Arctic”; most countries now recognize the Southern Ocean as the fifth; the ocean covers 71 percent of the Earth.
sources.zh: 全世界只有一個海洋；過去有四個命名的大洋；多數國家承認南大洋；海洋覆蓋 71%
sources.src: NOAA National Ocean Service, “How many oceans are there?”

sources.en: National Geographic recognized the Southern Ocean starting June 8, 2021; it had recognized four oceans since 1915; the U.S. Board on Geographic Names “has used the name since 1999”; the IHO used the name in 1937 and “repealed that designation in 1953.”
sources.zh: 國家地理學會 2021 年 6 月 8 日起承認南大洋；美國地名委員會 1999 年起使用
sources.src: National Geographic, “There's a new ocean now—can you name all five?” (June 8, 2021)

sources.en: “The Assembly approved the proposed IHO Resolution on the recognition of the Southern Ocean” (3rd IHO Assembly, May 3, 2023); the northern limit is the parallel of 60°S; Argentina's position is annexed.
sources.zh: 2023 年國際水文組織大會通過承認南大洋的決議，北界南緯 60 度
sources.src: International Hydrographic Organization, 3rd Assembly, summary record of the fourth plenary session

sources.en: Drafts of a fourth edition of Limits of Oceans and Seas (S-23) in 1986 and 2002 were not completed; the third edition dates from 1953.
sources.zh: 《海洋與海的界限》第四版草案（1986、2002）未完成；第三版是 1953 年
sources.src: International Hydrographic Organization, “Future of S-23” (Assembly-2 proposal, 2020)

sources.en: Areas of the continents: Asia 44,614,000, Africa 30,365,000, North America 24,230,000, South America 17,814,000 square kilometers; Antarctica about 14.2 million; Europe about 10 million (each continent's article, read October 2026).
sources.zh: 各洲面積（大英百科各洲條目，2026 年 10 月查閱）
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, articles “Asia,” “Africa,” “North America,” “South America,” “Antarctica,” “Europe”

sources.en: Area of Australia and Oceania, 8,510,926 square kilometers, from the table of continents, which adds up Britannica's figures.
sources.zh: 澳洲與大洋洲的面積
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Continent” (table of land areas)

sources.en: The Pacific, “excluding the South China Sea,” covers about 161.76 million square kilometers; the Atlantic without its dependent seas about 81,760,000; the Indian Ocean 70,560,000 without its marginal seas; the Arctic Ocean 14,090,000; the Southern Ocean 21,960,000 below 60°S (read October 2026).
sources.zh: 各大洋面積（大英百科各大洋條目，2026 年 10 月查閱）
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, articles “Pacific Ocean,” “Atlantic Ocean,” “Indian Ocean,” “Arctic Ocean,” “Southern Ocean”

sources.en: The Olympic symbol “represents the union of the five continents and the meeting of athletes from throughout the world at the Olympic Games” (Olympic Charter, Rule 8).
sources.zh: 奧林匹克憲章第 8 條：五環代表五大洲的團結
sources.src: International Olympic Committee, “Olympic rings”

sources.en: Zealandia: “A 4.9 Mkm2 region of the southwest Pacific Ocean is made up of continental crust”; “Today it is 94% submerged.”
sources.zh: 西蘭大陸：490 萬平方公里的大陸地殼，94% 在海面下
sources.src: Mortimer et al., “Zealandia: Earth's Hidden Continent,” GSA Today 27 (3), 2017

sources.en: Not everyone is convinced that Zealandia counts as a continent.
sources.zh: 不是每個人都同意西蘭大陸算一個洲
sources.src: National Geographic, “Lost continent hidden underneath New Zealand” (February 17, 2017)

sources.en: 「臺灣本島及其21個附屬島嶼面積共3萬5,887.1325平方公里」；「臺灣東臨太平洋」；「居東亞島弧中央」.
sources.zh: 台灣本島及 21 個附屬島嶼面積；東臨太平洋；位在東亞島弧中央
sources.src: 行政院，〈國情簡介：土地〉（資料來源內政部，114 年 5 月 28 日）

sources.en: Chinese terms: the Arctic Ocean appears as both 北冰洋 and 北極海; the Southern Ocean appears as 南大洋, 南冰洋, and 南極洋 in different fields.
sources.zh: 北冰洋／北極海；南大洋／南冰洋／南極洋
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，樂詞網

sources.en: 地 Aa-Ⅳ-2「全球海陸分布。」；地 Aa-Ⅳ-3；社 Ab-Ⅲ-1.
sources.zh: 社會領域課程綱要
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要：社會領域》（民國 107 年）

lessons.title: Why Is It Hot at the Equator and Cold at the Poles?
lessons.blurb_en: Shine the same beam of sunlight on a 3D Earth and move it from the equator toward the poles. Watch the bright patch stretch out, and see why slanted sunlight warms the ground less.
lessons.blurb_zh: 把同一束陽光照在 3D 地球上，從赤道往兩極移動，看地上的光斑越拉越長，了解為什麼斜斜的陽光比較不會把地面曬熱。
lessons.big_idea_en: Near the equator, sunlight comes down almost straight, so its energy is packed into a small area. Toward the poles, the same sunlight arrives at a slant and is spread over a much larger area, so each square meter gets less. That is the main reason the equator is hot and the poles are cold.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 在赤道附近，陽光幾乎是直直照下來，能量集中在一小塊地面；越往兩極，同樣的陽光斜斜地照進來，攤在大得多的面積上，每平方公尺分到的就比較少。這是赤道熱、兩極冷的主要原因。

lab.how_en: A square beam of sunlight shines on the Earth along 121 degrees east, the line that passes through Taiwan. Move it north or south with the slider, or tap the globe. The gold patch shows where the beam lands, and the number tells you how many times larger it is than the pale overhead patch. Change the season to move the overhead Sun between the tropics, and turn on the colored bands to see the five zones.
lab.how_zh: 一束截面是正方形的陽光，沿著東經 121 度（經過台灣的那條經線）照在地球上。用滑桿或點地球，把它往北或往南移。金色的光斑是光束落地的地方，數字告訴你它是淡色的直射光斑的幾倍大。換季節，太陽直射的地方就在南北回歸線之間移動；打開色帶，可以看到五帶。

legend.en: Five zones: tropical, two temperate, two polar
legend.zh: 五帶：熱帶、南北溫帶、南北寒帶

lab.scale_en: The beam is drawn much wider than real sunlight needs to be, so you can see it. The zones are the simple version bounded by the tropics and the polar circles; real climates also depend on oceans, winds, mountains, and height above sea level.
lab.scale_zh: 光束畫得比實際需要的寬很多，才看得清楚。五帶是用回歸線與極圈劃分的簡化版本；真實的氣候還和海洋、風、山脈、海拔有關。
lab.credit_html: Land outlines: Natural Earth, 1:50m Land, version 5.1.2, public domain. The Sun's height, the size of the patch, and the zones are computed by the page itself. · 陸地外形：Natural Earth 1:50m Land 5.1.2 版，公有領域。太陽高度、光斑大小與五帶都由頁面自己計算。

overhead.en: The Sun is straight overhead at noon here. The beam lands on the smallest possible patch, so the ground gets the most energy.
overhead.zh: 這裡正午太陽在頭頂正上方。光束落在最小的一塊地面上，地面分到的能量最多。

slant.en: The sunlight arrives at a slant, so the same beam covers a larger patch. Each square meter gets less of it.
slant.zh: 陽光斜斜地照進來，同一束光蓋住比較大的一塊地面，每平方公尺分到的比較少。

low.en: The noon Sun is barely above the horizon. The beam grazes the ground and spreads out enormously.
low.zh: 正午的太陽只比地平線高一點點。光束幾乎是擦過地面，攤得非常開。

night.en: Here the Sun does not rise even at noon at this time of year. This is the polar night.
night.zh: 每年這個時候，這裡連正午太陽都不會升起，這就是極夜。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four places to put the beam

parts.text_en: In March the Sun is overhead at the equator. The beam lands on its smallest patch: × 1.
parts.text_zh: 三月時太陽直射赤道。光束落在最小的光斑上：× 1。

parts.text_en: Move the beam to northern Taiwan. The noon Sun is 65 degrees high, and the patch is a little larger.
parts.text_zh: 把光束移到台灣北部。正午太陽高度 65 度，光斑大了一點。

parts.text_en: At 60 degrees north the noon Sun is only 30 degrees high in March. The same beam spreads over more than twice the area.
parts.text_zh: 三月時，北緯 60 度的正午太陽只有 30 度高。同一束光攤開成兩倍多的面積。

parts.en: Overhead at the Tropic of Cancer
parts.text_en: In June the overhead Sun moves north to the Tropic of Cancer, which crosses Taiwan. The whole pattern of sunlight shifts north.
parts.text_zh: 六月時，太陽直射點北移到穿過台灣的北回歸線，整個陽光分布都往北移。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Choose December and move the beam to 70 degrees north. What happens, and why?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。選十二月，把光束移到北緯 70 度。發生了什麼事？為什麼？

torch.en: Shine a Flashlight on the Table
torch.lead_en: The same flashlight, straight down or at a slant. Drag the angle and compare the two pictures: the beam does not change, but the patch on the table does.
torch.lead_zh: 同一支手電筒，從正上方照或斜斜地照。拖動角度，比較兩張圖：光束沒有變，桌上的光斑變了。
torch.note_en: At 30 degrees the patch is twice as long, so each square gets half the light. That is what happens to sunlight far from the equator.
torch.note_zh: 30 度時光斑變成兩倍長，所以每一格只分到一半的光。離赤道越遠，陽光就是這樣。

sunq.lead_en: Eight questions. Each one gives two places and a time of year. Where is the noon Sun higher in the sky? You do not need to memorize anything: the closer a place is to the latitude where the Sun is overhead, the higher its noon Sun. There is no timer.
sunq.lead_zh: 八道題。每一題給兩個地方和一個季節：哪裡正午的太陽比較高？不用背任何東西：離太陽直射的緯度越近，正午的太陽就越高。不計時。
sunq.hint_en: First find where the Sun is overhead. Then ask: which place is closer to that latitude?
sunq.hint_zh: 先找出太陽直射哪裡，再問：哪個地方離那條緯線比較近？
sunq.start_en: Closer to the overhead Sun means a higher Sun.
sunq.start_zh: 離太陽直射的地方越近，太陽越高。
sunq.end_en: Now you can work out where the Sun is high and where it is low, in any season.
sunq.end_zh: 現在你可以推算任何季節裡，哪裡的太陽高、哪裡的太陽低。

questions.why_en: In March the Sun is overhead at the equator. Singapore is almost on the equator; Reykjavík is far to the north.
questions.why_zh: 三月太陽直射赤道。新加坡幾乎就在赤道上，雷克雅維克遠在北方。

questions.why_en: Taipei is much closer to the equator than London.
questions.why_zh: 台北比倫敦離赤道近得多。

questions.why_en: In June the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, just south of Taipei. Taipei is closer to it than Singapore is.
questions.why_zh: 六月太陽直射北回歸線，就在台北南邊不遠。台北比新加坡離它更近。

questions.why_en: In December the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn, in the south. Sydney is much closer to it.
questions.why_zh: 十二月太陽直射南方的南回歸線。雪梨離它近得多。

questions.why_en: In March the Sun is over the equator. Cairo is 30 degrees north and Durban is about 30 degrees south: the same distance away.
questions.why_zh: 三月太陽直射赤道。開羅在北緯 30 度，德班大約在南緯 30 度：離赤道一樣遠。

questions.why_en: Even in June, London is farther from the Tropic of Cancer than Singapore is.
questions.why_zh: 即使在六月，倫敦離北回歸線也比新加坡遠。

questions.why_en: In December the overhead Sun is far to the south. Reykjavík's noon Sun barely clears the horizon, while Ushuaia's is high.
questions.why_zh: 十二月太陽直射點在遙遠的南方。雷克雅維克的正午太陽只比地平線高一點點，烏斯懷亞的卻很高。

questions.why_en: In June the overhead Sun is in the north. London is closer to the Tropic of Cancer than Sydney is.
questions.why_zh: 六月太陽直射點在北方。倫敦比雪梨離北回歸線近。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about sunlight and climate
map_english.zh: 談陽光與氣候的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about sunlight and latitude. Listen, repeat, then describe how high the Sun is where you live.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說陽光和緯度。先聽、再跟著唸，然後描述你住的地方太陽有多高。

items.en: The Sun is high in the sky near the equator.
items.zh: 在赤道附近，太陽高掛在天空。

items.en: Near the poles, sunlight is spread out over a larger area.
items.zh: 在兩極附近，陽光攤在比較大的面積上。

items.en: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Taiwan.
items.zh: 北回歸線穿過台灣。

items.en: In June, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.
items.zh: 六月時，太陽直射北回歸線。

items.en: The closer you are to the equator, the warmer it usually is.
items.zh: 離赤道越近，通常就越溫暖。

items.en: In winter, sunlight hits the ground at a low angle.
items.zh: 冬天時，陽光以很低的角度照在地面上。

items.en: Southern Taiwan is in the tropical zone.
items.zh: 台灣南部在熱帶。

items.en: How high is the Sun at noon today?
items.zh: 今天正午的太陽有多高？

tricks_head.en: Sunlight and latitude in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住陽光與緯度

tricks.body_en: Slanted light spreads out, so each square meter gets less.
tricks.body_zh: 斜射的光會攤開，每平方公尺分到的比較少。

tricks.title_zh: 離直射點越近，太陽越高
tricks.body_en: Noon Sun height = 90 − the distance in degrees from where the Sun is overhead.
tricks.body_zh: 正午太陽高度＝90 − 和直射點相差幾度。

tricks.title_en: The overhead Sun stays between the tropics
tricks.title_zh: 直射點只在回歸線之間
tricks.body_en: It moves north to the Tropic of Cancer in June and south to the Tropic of Capricorn in December.
tricks.body_zh: 六月北移到北回歸線，十二月南移到南回歸線。

tricks.body_en: Two tropics and two polar circles divide the Earth into five zones.
tricks.body_zh: 兩條回歸線、兩條極圈，把地球分成五帶。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Never look straight at the Sun, and never look at it through a lens, binoculars, or a phone camera.
safety.zh: 絕對不要直視太陽，也不要透過鏡片、望遠鏡或手機鏡頭看太陽。

safety.en: Do not shine a flashlight into anyone's eyes.
safety.zh: 不要拿手電筒照別人的眼睛。

safety.en: When you measure shadows outside, stay where your teacher can see you, drink water, and wear a hat in strong sun.
safety.zh: 到戶外量影子時，待在老師看得到的地方，記得喝水，太陽大時戴帽子。

safety.en: Push the stick into soft ground or a pot of sand with care, and do not leave it where someone could trip over it.
safety.zh: 把棍子小心插進軟土或一盆沙裡，不要放在別人可能絆倒的地方。

materials.en: A flashlight
Graph paper
A protractor
A pencil and a ruler

steps.en: Darken the room a little. Hold the flashlight straight above the graph paper, about 20 centimeters away.
steps.zh: 把教室弄暗一點。手電筒拿在方格紙正上方，大約 20 公分高。

steps.en: Trace the edge of the bright patch and count the squares inside it.
steps.zh: 沿著亮的光斑描邊，數一數裡面有幾格。

steps.en: Keep the same distance, and tilt the flashlight to about 30 degrees from the paper. Use the protractor to check.
steps.zh: 保持一樣的距離，把手電筒傾斜到和紙面大約 30 度，用量角器檢查。

steps.en: Trace the patch again and count the squares. How many times larger is it?
steps.zh: 再描一次光斑、數格子。它大了幾倍？

steps.en: Which patch looked brighter? Write one sentence that connects this to the equator and the poles.
steps.zh: 哪一個光斑看起來比較亮？寫一句話，把它和赤道、兩極連起來。

activities.tip_en: The flashlight gives out the same light both times. Only the angle changes, and so does the size of the patch.
activities.tip_zh: 兩次手電筒發出的光一樣多，改變的只有角度，還有光斑的大小。

activities.title_en: How High Is the Noon Sun?

materials.en: A straight stick about 1 meter long, or a pencil standing in clay
materials.zh: 一根大約 1 公尺長的直棍子，或插在黏土上的鉛筆

materials.en: A measuring tape
A sunny, flat place
A calculator, or the table your teacher gives you
materials.zh: 計算機，或老師給的對照表

steps.en: Stand the stick straight up on flat ground. Measure its height above the ground.
steps.zh: 把棍子直直地立在平地上，量它露出地面的高度。

steps.en: Close to noon, measure the length of its shadow. Do not look at the Sun; look only at the shadow.
steps.zh: 接近正午時，量它影子的長度。不要看太陽，只看影子。

steps.en: Divide the height by the shadow length. Use a calculator's inverse tangent, or your teacher's table, to turn this into the Sun's height in degrees.
steps.zh: 用高度除以影子長度。用計算機的反正切，或老師給的對照表，換算成太陽高度幾度。

steps.en: Compare your answer with the 3D model: choose the season and move the beam to your latitude.
steps.zh: 和 3D 模型比一比：選季節，再把光束移到你所在的緯度。

steps.en: Repeat once a month. Does the noon shadow get longer or shorter as winter comes?
steps.zh: 每個月做一次。冬天快到時，正午的影子變長還是變短？

activities.tip_en: A long noon shadow means a low Sun and slanted sunlight. A short shadow means a high Sun.
activities.tip_zh: 正午影子長，表示太陽低、陽光斜；影子短，表示太陽高。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The Sun's height, the size of the patch, and the answers to the game are computed by the page itself and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；太陽高度、光斑大小與小遊戲的答案都由頁面自己計算，並有自動測試
paras: Stand in the sunshine at noon on a summer day, and you can feel the heat on your skin. Stand in the same sunshine late in the afternoon, and it feels much gentler, even though it is the same Sun. What changed is the angle of the light. The same idea explains why the lands near the equator are hot and the lands near the poles are cold.

Try it with a flashlight. Shine it straight down at a table, and you get a small, bright spot. Tilt it, and the light stretches into a longer, dimmer patch. The flashlight gives out the same amount of light both times. When it is tilted, that light is spread over more of the table, so each part of the table gets less.

Sunlight reaches the round Earth in the same way. Near the equator, the noon Sun is high and its rays come down almost straight. Toward the poles, the Earth curves away, and the same sunlight arrives at a slant. NASA explains that from the equator to the poles, sunlight meets the Earth at smaller and smaller angles, and “the light gets spread over larger and larger surface areas.” Slanted sunlight also travels a longer path through the air before it reaches the ground.

The Earth's axis is tilted, so the place where the noon Sun is straight overhead moves during the year. In June it is over the Tropic of Cancer, about 23.4 degrees north. In December it is over the Tropic of Capricorn, about 23.4 degrees south. Outside the tropics, the noon Sun is never straight overhead. Beyond the Arctic and Antarctic Circles, there are days in winter when the Sun does not rise at all.

These four lines divide the Earth into five zones: the tropical zone between the two tropics, two temperate zones, and two polar zones beyond the polar circles. Real climates are more complicated, because oceans, winds, mountains, and height above sea level all make a difference. But the angle of sunlight is the starting point.

The Tropic of Cancer crosses Taiwan, passing through Chiayi, Hualien, and Penghu. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration says this is why southern Taiwan is tropical and northern Taiwan is subtropical. In June, the noon Sun stands almost straight above the Tropic of Cancer markers. When you feel the summer sun in Taiwan, you are feeling sunlight that is nearly as direct as sunlight can be.
paras_zh: 夏天中午站在太陽下，你可以感覺到皮膚上的熱；傍晚站在同樣的陽光下，感覺就溫和多了，雖然還是同一個太陽。改變的是光照下來的角度。同樣的道理，可以解釋為什麼赤道附近的地方熱、兩極附近的地方冷。
用手電筒試試看。從正上方照桌子，會照出一個又小又亮的光點；斜著照，光就拉長成一塊比較長、比較暗的光斑。兩次手電筒發出的光一樣多，斜著照的時候，同樣的光攤在比較多的桌面上，所以桌子的每一部分分到的就比較少。
陽光照在圓圓的地球上也是這樣。在赤道附近，正午的太陽很高，陽光幾乎是直直照下來；越往兩極，地面越往遠處彎，同樣的陽光就斜斜地照進來。NASA 說明：從赤道到兩極，陽光和地面的夾角越來越小，「光攤在越來越大的面積上」。斜射的陽光在到達地面之前，穿過的空氣也比較長。
地球的自轉軸是傾斜的，所以一年當中，正午太陽直射的地方會移動。六月時直射北回歸線，大約北緯 23.4 度；十二月時直射南回歸線，大約南緯 23.4 度。在回歸線以外的地方，正午的太陽永遠不會在頭頂正上方。在北極圈、南極圈以內，冬天會有太陽整天都不升起的日子。
這四條線把地球分成五帶：兩條回歸線之間的熱帶、兩個溫帶，以及極圈以內的兩個寒帶。真實的氣候比較複雜，海洋、風、山脈和海拔高度都有影響；但陽光的角度是起點。
北回歸線穿過台灣，經過嘉義、花蓮和澎湖。中央氣象署說，因為這樣，台灣南部屬熱帶、北部屬副熱帶。六月時，正午的太陽幾乎就在北回歸線標誌的正上方。當你在台灣感受到夏天的太陽，你感受到的，幾乎是最直的陽光了。
questions: Why does a tilted flashlight make a dimmer patch, even though it gives out the same light?
Why is the noon Sun never straight overhead in London or Reykjavík?
Besides the angle of sunlight, what else can make one place warmer or colder than another at the same latitude?
answers: The same light is spread over a larger area, so each part of the table gets less of it.
The overhead Sun only moves between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, and both cities are far north of the Tropic of Cancer.
Oceans, winds, mountains, and height above sea level. For example, high mountains are colder than the lowlands around them.

vocab.ex: Singapore is very close to the equator.
vocab.exzh: 新加坡離赤道很近。

vocab.ex: The poles get slanted sunlight all year.
vocab.exzh: 兩極一整年得到的都是斜射的陽光。

vocab.ex: The angle of sunlight changes with the seasons.
vocab.exzh: 陽光的角度隨季節改變。

vocab.ex: Direct sunlight heats the ground quickly.
vocab.exzh: 直射的陽光很快就把地面曬熱。

vocab.ex: Slanted sunlight spreads over a larger area.
vocab.exzh: 斜射的陽光攤在比較大的面積上。

vocab.ex: The light spreads out when you tilt the flashlight.
vocab.exzh: 把手電筒斜過來，光就攤開了。

myths.myth_en: The poles are cold because they are farther from the Sun.
myths.myth_zh: 兩極冷，是因為離太陽比較遠。
myths.fact_en: The angle of sunlight matters, not the distance. The Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January, during the northern winter.
myths.fact_zh: 重要的是陽光的角度，不是距離。地球其實在一月離太陽最近，那時北半球是冬天。

myths.myth_en: At the equator, the noon Sun is straight overhead every day.
myths.myth_zh: 赤道上，每天正午太陽都在頭頂正上方。
myths.fact_en: The overhead Sun moves between the tropics during the year. It passes over the equator only around March and September.
myths.fact_zh: 太陽直射點一年當中在南北回歸線之間移動，只有在三月和九月前後才經過赤道。

myths.myth_en: Slanted sunlight is weaker because the Sun gives out less light.
myths.myth_zh: 斜射的陽光比較弱，是因為太陽發出的光比較少。
myths.fact_en: The Sun sends the same light. Slanted light is spread over more ground, so each square meter gets less.
myths.fact_zh: 太陽發出的光一樣多；斜射的光攤在比較多的地面上，每平方公尺分到的比較少。

myths.myth_en: Places in the polar zones never see the Sun in summer.
myths.myth_zh: 寒帶的地方夏天也看不到太陽。
myths.fact_en: In summer the Sun can stay up all day and all night there. It is low in the sky, so its light is slanted.
myths.fact_zh: 夏天時，那裡的太陽可以整天整夜都不落下；只是太陽很低，光是斜的。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Lines · 線背後的故事

cards.k: About 276–194 BCE · Eratosthenes · 埃拉托斯特尼
cards.en: Sunlight at the bottom of a well
cards.body_en: The Greek geographer Eratosthenes read that a deep well near Syene, in southern Egypt, was lit all the way down at noon once a year, so the Sun had to be straight overhead. In Alexandria, farther north, posts still cast shadows that day. From the difference he estimated the size of the Earth.
cards.body_zh: 希臘地理學家埃拉托斯特尼讀到：埃及南部賽伊尼附近有一口深井，每年有一天正午陽光會照到井底，所以那時太陽一定在正上方。同一天，北邊亞歷山卓的柱子還有影子。他從這個差別估算出地球有多大。

cards.body_en: At the June solstice the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer. Long ago, the Sun appeared in the constellation Cancer at that time, which gave the line its name. Today it appears in Gemini, because the direction of the Earth's axis slowly changes.
cards.body_zh: 六月夏至時，太陽直射北回歸線。很久以前，那時太陽出現在巨蟹座，這條線就因此得名（英文叫「巨蟹的回歸線」）。今天那時太陽出現在雙子座，因為地球自轉軸的方向會慢慢改變。

cards.body_en: The Tropic of Cancer is not fixed. A monument in Chiayi City says it moves south by more than 14 meters a year, and that in 1788 it passed near what is now the corner of Boai Road and Shixian Road. Chiayi City's marker, opened on June 21, 2004, is counted as the world's tenth Tropic of Cancer marker.
cards.body_zh: 北回歸線不是固定不動的。嘉義市的碑文說，它每年往南移動 14 公尺多，西元 1788 年通過今天博愛路與世賢路口北端附近。嘉義市的標誌在 2004 年 6 月 21 日落成，是「全球北回歸線標誌第十處」。

cards.en: From one day to six months
cards.body_en: On the Arctic Circle, the Sun stays up all day for about one day each June and stays down for about one day each December. Farther north, these stretches grow longer, until at the North Pole there are six months of daylight and six months of night.
cards.body_zh: 在北極圈上，每年六月大約有一天太陽整天不落下，十二月大約有一天太陽整天不升起。越往北，這樣的日子越長；到了北極，是半年的白天和半年的黑夜。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum (2018). The main idea of this lesson is written almost word for word in junior high natural science. The curriculum does not use the term solar altitude angle; it speaks of the angle of sunlight.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要（民國 107 年發布）。這一課的核心幾乎原原本本寫在國中自然科學裡。課綱沒有用「太陽高度角」這個詞，用的是「陽光照射角度」。

items.text: 陽光照射角度之變化，會造成地表單位面積土地吸收太陽能量的不同。
items.note_en: This is the lesson's big idea. The flashlight activity and the 3D beam show it directly.
items.note_zh: 這正是本課的核心。手電筒活動和 3D 光束直接示範這件事。

items.text: 地球的四季主要是因為地球自轉軸傾斜於地球公轉軌道面而造成。
items.note_en: The season buttons move the overhead Sun between the tropics.
items.note_zh: 季節按鈕讓太陽直射點在南北回歸線之間移動。

items.text: 臺灣的氣候特色。
items.note_en: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Taiwan: southern Taiwan is tropical and northern Taiwan subtropical.
items.note_zh: 北回歸線穿過台灣：南部屬熱帶、北部屬副熱帶。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 日出日落時間與位置，在不同季節會不同。
items.note_en: Measuring the noon shadow each month shows the Sun's path changing with the seasons.
items.note_zh: 每個月量一次正午的影子，就能看出太陽的路徑隨季節改變。

sources.en: “From the equator to the poles, the Sun's rays meet Earth at smaller and smaller angles, and the light gets spread over larger and larger surface areas.”
sources.zh: 從赤道到兩極，陽光和地面的夾角越來越小，光攤在越來越大的面積上
sources.src: NASA Earth Observatory, “Climate and Earth's Energy Budget,” page 2

sources.en: The farther from the equator the radiation strikes, “the more of an angle it has, spreading the energy over a larger area.”
sources.zh: 離赤道越遠，陽光越斜，能量攤在越大的面積上
sources.src: NOAA JetStream, “Tropical Weather Systems”

sources.en: With a high Sun, “less sunlight gets scattered before reaching the ground because it has less distance to travel through the atmosphere”; the Earth is closest to the Sun in January, and “this distance change is not great enough to cause any substantial difference in our climate.”
sources.zh: 太陽高時穿過的大氣比較短；地球一月離太陽最近，距離變化不足以造成氣候的明顯差別
sources.src: National Weather Service, Sioux Falls, “What Causes the Seasons?”

sources.en: Solstices are defined by solar declination, “the latitude of Earth where the sun is directly overhead at noon”; about 23.5°N (Tropic of Cancer) in June and 23.5°S (Tropic of Capricorn) in December.
sources.zh: 太陽直射的緯度；六月北回歸線、十二月南回歸線
sources.src: National Geographic Education, “Solstice”

sources.en: “The Tropic of Cancer, for instance, is 23 degrees 26 minutes 21 seconds N.” The model uses 23.44 degrees.
sources.zh: 北回歸線在北緯 23 度 26 分 21 秒（模型用 23.44 度）
sources.src: National Geographic Encyclopedia, “Latitude”

sources.en: The Tropic of Cancer was named when the Sun lay in the constellation Cancer at the June solstice; it now appears in Gemini (read November 2026).
sources.zh: 北回歸線因為從前夏至時太陽在巨蟹座而得名，現在在雙子座
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Tropic of Cancer”

sources.en: The Arctic Circle, at approximately 66°30′ N, marks the southern limit of the area where the Sun does not set (about June 21) or rise (about December 21) for one day or more; continuous day or night grows from one day on the circle to six months at the pole (read November 2026).
sources.zh: 北極圈：至少一天太陽不落或不升；在北極是半年
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Arctic Circle”

sources.en: “During a cycle that averages about 40,000 years, the tilt of the axis varies between 22.1 and 24.5 degrees.”
sources.zh: 地軸傾角在 22.1 到 24.5 度之間變化，週期約四萬年
sources.src: NASA Earth Observatory, “Milankovitch (Orbital) Cycles”

sources.en: Eratosthenes (about 276 to 194 B.C.) read that a deep vertical well near Syene “was entirely lit up by the Sun at noon once a year” and reasoned that the Sun must be directly overhead.
sources.zh: 埃拉托斯特尼與賽伊尼的井
sources.src: NOAA JetStream, “Learning Lesson: The Shadow Knows I”

sources.en: 「北回歸線以每年14公尺餘的速度向南移動，於西元1788年通過本市博愛路與世賢路路口北端附近」；「全球北回歸線標誌第十處」, opened June 21, 2004; the markers divide 「北寒帶、北溫帶、熱帶、南溫帶、南寒帶等五帶」.
sources.zh: 嘉義市北回歸線標誌與碑文
sources.src: 交通部觀光署，〈全球北回歸線標誌第十處〉

sources.en: 「北回歸線通過花蓮、嘉義、澎湖３縣境，故南部屬熱帶，北部屬副熱帶。」
sources.zh: 台灣南部屬熱帶、北部屬副熱帶
sources.src: 中央氣象署南區氣象中心，〈臺灣的氣候〉

sources.en: Chinese terms: 太陽高度角／太陽高度 (solar altitude), 斜射 (oblique incidence), 寒帶 (frigid zone), 北回歸線 (Tropic of Cancer).
sources.zh: 名詞
sources.src: 國家教育研究院，樂詞網

lessons.title: Where Do People Live?
lessons.blurb_en: Cover a 3D Earth with one dot for every million people, then hunt for the crowded places and the empty ones. Find out why water, flat land, and a gentle climate draw people together.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球上，每一百萬人放一個點，找找哪裡擠滿了人、哪裡幾乎沒有人。看看為什麼水、平地和溫和的氣候會把人聚在一起。
lessons.big_idea_en: People are spread very unevenly over the Earth. Most people live where there is water, flat land, and a climate that is neither too dry nor too cold. Deserts, high mountains, and the polar zones have very few people.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 人在地球上分布得非常不平均。大多數人住在有水、有平地、氣候不太乾也不太冷的地方；沙漠、高山和寒帶住的人非常少。

lab.how_en: Each gold dot stands for one million people, from a population grid for the year 2025. Turn the globe and look for the crowded places and the empty ones. Choose an area on the right, such as the large deserts, to see what share of the land it covers and what share of the people live there. Tap anywhere on the globe to see about how many people live in that 1° × 1° square.
lab.how_zh: 每一個金色的點代表一百萬人，資料是 2025 年的人口格網。轉動地球，找找哪裡擠滿了人、哪裡幾乎是空的。在右邊選一種地方，例如大沙漠，看它占陸地面積的幾成、住了全世界幾成的人。點地球上任何一個地方，看那個 1 度 × 1 度的格子裡大約住了多少人。

legend.zh: 點選的 1 度 × 1 度格子

lab.scale_en: A dot shows roughly where a million people live, not an exact town: each dot is placed inside its 1° square according to where people live in the data. The desert outlines are rough areas from Natural Earth, and the high land comes from an old, coarse elevation grid, so both are only approximate.
lab.scale_zh: 一個點只表示一百萬人大約住在哪一帶，不是某一個城鎮：每個點依資料裡人住的地方，放在它那個 1 度格子裡。沙漠的範圍是 Natural Earth 的大約範圍，高地取自很舊、很粗的高度資料，都只是大約。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The dots pile up on the plains and river valleys of South and East Asia, Taiwan included. More than half of the world's people live in Asia.
parts.text_zh: 點在南亞和東亞的平原、河谷堆成一片，台灣也在其中。全世界超過一半的人住在亞洲。

parts.text_en: The Sahara is almost empty, but a thin line of dots follows the Nile north to its delta. Water makes the difference.
parts.text_zh: 撒哈拉幾乎是空的，但一條細細的點沿著尼羅河往北，一直到三角洲。差別就在水。

parts.text_en: The Plateau of Tibet is high, cold, and dry. Land above 3,000 meters covers about 3% of the land but holds only about 0.5% of the people. Right next to it, the plains to the south are among the most crowded places on Earth.
parts.text_zh: 青藏高原又高、又冷、又乾。海拔 3,000 公尺以上的地方大約占陸地的 3%，只住了大約 0.5% 的人；緊鄰在南邊的平原，卻是地球上人最擠的地方之一。

parts.text_en: Beyond the polar circles, where Lesson 7 showed the sunlight is always slanted, there is hardly a dot. Only about 0.02% of the world's people live there.
parts.text_zh: 在極圈以內（第七課看過，那裡的陽光永遠是斜的）幾乎看不到點，只住了全世界大約 0.02% 的人。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Find the empty space in the middle of Australia, and the crowded line of dots along its eastern coast. Why are they so different?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。找出澳洲中部那一大片空白，和沿著東部海岸擠在一起的點。為什麼差這麼多？

why.lead_en: Eight places. Each card tells you about the water, the land, and the climate. Decide whether many people or few people live there, then check your answer against the population data. You do not need to memorize anything: think about what people need. There is no timer.
why.lead_zh: 八個地方。每一張卡告訴你那裡的水、地形和氣候。判斷那裡住的人很多還是很少，再用人口資料對答案。不用背任何東西：想想人需要什麼。不計時。
why.hint_en: Ask three questions: Is there water? Is the land flat and low? Is the climate gentle enough to grow food?
why.hint_zh: 問三個問題：有沒有水？地是不是又平又低？氣候溫和到可以種糧食嗎？
why.start_en: Water, flat land, and a gentle climate bring people together.
why.start_zh: 水、平地、溫和的氣候，會把人聚在一起。
why.end_en: Now you can look at any place on a map and guess whether many people live there, and why.
why.end_zh: 現在你可以看著地圖上任何一個地方，猜那裡人多還是人少，還說得出原因。

chips.en: A great river and its delta
chips.zh: 一條大河和它的三角洲

questions.why_en: It almost never rains, but the river brings water to flat, rich land. People have crowded along it and in its delta.
questions.why_zh: 這裡幾乎不下雨，但河水流過平坦肥沃的土地，人就沿著河、在三角洲擠在一起。

questions.why_en: Without water there are no farms, and without farms very few people can live there.
questions.why_zh: 沒有水就不能種田，不能種田，能住在這裡的人就非常少。

chips.zh: 幾條大河和它們的三角洲

questions.why_en: Water, flat land, and warm weather: everything farmers need. It is one of the most crowded places on Earth.
questions.why_zh: 有水、有平地、天氣溫暖：農夫需要的都有了。這裡是地球上人最擠的地方之一。

chips.zh: 河流在這裡才剛開始，是小溪

questions.why_en: High land is cold, the air is thin, and the growing season is short. Few people live up here.
questions.why_zh: 地勢高就冷，空氣稀薄，能種東西的時間很短。住在這上面的人很少。

questions.why_en: Nothing can grow on an ice sheet. Almost nobody lives in the middle of it.
questions.why_zh: 冰原上什麼都長不出來，冰原中央幾乎沒有人住。

chips.en: Flat land around rich volcanic soil

questions.why_en: Plenty of water, rich soil, and warm weather all year: this island is packed with people.
questions.why_zh: 水多、土壤肥沃、一年到頭都溫暖：這座島上擠滿了人。

chips.en: Flat, but covered by thick forest
chips.zh: 地很平，但長滿濃密的森林

questions.why_en: This one is tricky. There is water and the land is flat, but thick rainforest and poor soil make farming hard, and travel is slow. Few people live deep in the forest.
questions.why_zh: 這一題比較難。有水、地也平，但濃密的雨林和貧瘠的土壤讓種田很難，交通也慢。住在雨林深處的人很少。

chips.en: Short rivers and plenty of rain

chips.zh: 溫暖，介於熱帶和副熱帶

questions.why_en: Taiwan's western plains have water, flat land, and a warm climate. Millions of people live in this one square.
questions.why_zh: 台灣西部平原有水、有平地、氣候溫暖。光是這一個格子裡就住了幾百萬人。

hundred.zh: 如果世界只有一百個人
hundred.lead_en: Shrink the whole world down to 100 people. Where would they live? Switch between regions of the world and bands of latitude, and tap a group to see the real numbers.
hundred.lead_zh: 把全世界縮小成一百個人，他們會住在哪裡？在「依地區」和「依緯度帶」之間切換，點一組看實際的數字。

src_regions.en: Regions and numbers: United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024 (mid-2025). Central America and the Caribbean are counted in Latin America, not in Northern America.
src_regions.zh: 地區與數字：聯合國《世界人口展望 2024》（2025 年年中）。中美洲與加勒比海算在「拉丁美洲與加勒比海」，不算在「北美洲（北部）」。

src_bands.en: Bands of latitude: computed by this page from the GHS-POP population grid for 2025.
src_bands.zh: 緯度帶：本頁用 GHS-POP 2025 年人口格網自己算的。

hundred.hint_en: Tap a group to see how many people it stands for.
hundred.hint_zh: 點一組，看它代表多少人。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about where people live
map_english.zh: 談人住在哪裡的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about population. Listen, repeat, then describe where people live in your county or city.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說人口與分布。先聽、再跟著唸，然後描述你住的縣市裡，人都住在哪裡。

items.en: Most people live on low, flat land.
items.zh: 大多數人住在又低又平的地方。

items.en: Few people live in the desert.
items.zh: 住在沙漠裡的人很少。

items.en: Many towns grew up along the river.
items.zh: 很多城鎮是沿著河流發展起來的。

items.en: Taiwan is densely populated.
items.zh: 台灣人口很稠密。

items.en: The population of Taiwan is about 23 million.
items.zh: 台灣的人口大約是兩千三百萬。

items.en: More than half of the world's people live in Asia.
items.zh: 全世界超過一半的人住在亞洲。

items.en: Each dot stands for one million people.
items.zh: 每一個點代表一百萬人。

items.en: How many people live in your town?
items.zh: 你住的城鎮有多少人？

tricks_head.en: Where people live, in a sentence
tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住人住在哪裡

tricks.body_en: Where these come together, people crowd together.
tricks.body_zh: 這三樣湊在一起的地方，人就擠在一起。

tricks.title_en: Too dry, too high, too cold
tricks.body_en: Deserts, high mountains, and the polar zones have few people.
tricks.body_zh: 沙漠、高山、寒帶，住的人很少。

tricks.title_zh: 人口密度＝人數 ÷ 面積
tricks.body_en: Count the people, divide by the square kilometers.
tricks.body_zh: 數人數，再除以幾平方公里。

tricks.body_en: Water can make even a desert crowded, like the Nile.
tricks.body_zh: 有水，連沙漠也會擠滿人，像尼羅河。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: When you measure the classroom or the playground, walk, do not run, and watch out for desks and chairs.
safety.zh: 量教室或操場時，用走的不要用跑的，小心桌椅。

safety.en: Stay where your teacher can see you when you work outside, and drink water on hot days.
safety.zh: 在戶外活動時，待在老師看得到的地方；天氣熱要記得喝水。

safety.en: Do not stand on chairs or desks to reach anything.
safety.zh: 不要站到椅子或桌子上拿東西。

safety.en: Count people by looking, not by touching or pushing. Be kind when you talk about crowded or poor places.
safety.zh: 數人用看的，不要碰或推別人。談到擁擠或貧窮的地方時，說話要尊重。

materials.en: A long measuring tape
Chalk or tape
A calculator
Paper and a pencil

steps.en: Measure the length and width of your classroom in meters. Multiply them to find the area in square meters.
steps.zh: 量教室的長和寬（公尺），相乘得到面積（平方公尺）。

steps.en: Count the people in the room. Divide the number of people by the area: that is the classroom's population density.
steps.zh: 數一數教室裡有幾個人。人數除以面積，就是教室的人口密度。

steps.en: Do the same for a part of the playground with the same number of people standing in it.
steps.zh: 在操場劃出一塊地，讓同樣多的人站進去，再算一次。

steps.en: Which place is more crowded? Write the two densities side by side.
steps.zh: 哪裡比較擠？把兩個密度並排寫下來。

steps.en: Taiwan has about 646 people per square kilometer (2024). Is your classroom more or less crowded than that? (One square kilometer is 1,000,000 square meters.)
steps.zh: 台灣每平方公里大約 646 人（民國 113 年）。你們的教室比這個擠，還是比較空？（一平方公里是 1,000,000 平方公尺。）

activities.tip_en: Population density does not count people one by one in each spot. It is an average: the same number can hide crowded corners and empty ones.
activities.tip_zh: 人口密度不是一個一個地方去數，而是平均：同一個數字，可能藏著很擠的角落和空空的角落。

activities.title_en: Where Would You Build a Village?

materials.en: A large sheet of paper
Colored pencils
20 small paper squares or beans
materials.zh: 20 張小紙片或 20 顆豆子

steps.en: In a group, draw an imaginary island with a river, a coast, a tall mountain, a dry sandy area, and a forest.
steps.zh: 分組，畫一座想像的島：有一條河、海岸、一座高山、一片乾燥的沙地和一片森林。

steps.en: Each square or bean is 1,000 people. Place all 20 where you think people would choose to live.
steps.zh: 每一張紙片或每一顆豆子代表 1,000 人。把 20 個都放在你覺得人會選擇住的地方。

steps.en: Write one reason for each crowded spot and each empty spot.
steps.zh: 每一個擠的地方、每一個空的地方，都寫一個理由。

steps.en: Compare your island with another group's. Did you crowd people in the same places?
steps.zh: 和另一組比一比，你們把人放在一樣的地方嗎？

steps.en: Now look at the 3D globe. Can you find real places that look like your island?
steps.zh: 再看 3D 地球：你找得到和你們的島很像的真實地方嗎？

activities.tip_en: There is no single right answer. Good answers explain the reason: water, flat land, climate, or a way to travel.
activities.tip_zh: 沒有唯一的正確答案；好的答案會說出理由：水、平地、氣候，或交通。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The dots, the shares of people and land, and the answers to the game are computed by the page itself from the population grid and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；點的位置、人口與陸地的比例、小遊戲的答案，都由頁面用人口格網自己計算，並有自動測試
paras: Imagine giving every person on Earth a seat on a giant map. In 2025, the United Nations estimates, there are about 8.23 billion of us. If people were spread out evenly, every piece of land would have its share. They are not. Some places are packed shoulder to shoulder, and enormous areas have almost nobody at all.

On the globe in this lesson, each dot stands for one million people. The dots crowd together in South Asia and East Asia, along the great rivers, and near many coasts. More than half of the world's people live in Asia. In the population data used here, about 86 out of every 100 people live north of the equator, partly because most of the world's land is in the Northern Hemisphere.

Why there? People need water to drink and to grow food. They need land that is flat enough to farm and to build on, and a climate that is neither too dry nor too cold. Rivers and coasts also make it easier to travel and to trade. Where water, flat land, and a gentle climate come together, villages grow into towns, and towns grow into cities.

Now look at the empty places. Deserts are too dry. High mountains and plateaus are cold, steep, and short of air. In the polar zones, as Lesson 7 showed, the sunlight is always slanted, and the ground may be frozen. The large deserts outlined on the globe cover about 10% of the land, but only about 2% of the world's people live in them, and most of those live along rivers such as the Nile. Land more than 3,000 meters high covers about 3% of the land and holds about 0.5% of the people.

Low land matters, too. A 1998 study found that about a third of the world's people lived less than 100 meters above sea level, even though only about a sixth of the land where people live is that low. The population and height data on this page give almost the same answer: about 34% of people on about 14% of the land. A 2016 study estimated that about 40 percent of people live within 100 kilometers of a coast.

To compare places, geographers use population density: the number of people divided by the area of land. Taiwan is one of the crowded places. In 2024, Taiwan had about 646 people per square kilometer, and Taipei City had more than 9,000. But even in Taiwan, people are not spread evenly: most live on the plains and in the basins, and few live high in the mountains.
paras_zh: 想像給地球上的每一個人在一張巨大的地圖上安排一個位子。聯合國估計，2025 年我們大約有 82.3 億人。如果人分布得很平均，每一塊陸地都會分到一份。事實不是這樣：有些地方擠得肩並肩，有些廣大的地方幾乎一個人都沒有。
在這一課的地球上，每一個點代表一百萬人。點擠在南亞和東亞、沿著大河、靠近許多海岸。全世界超過一半的人住在亞洲。在本課用的人口資料裡，每 100 個人大約有 86 個住在赤道以北，部分原因是地球上大部分的陸地在北半球。
為什麼是這些地方？人需要水來喝、來種糧食；需要夠平的地來耕種、蓋房子；也需要不太乾、不太冷的氣候。河流和海岸也讓交通和買賣比較方便。水、平地和溫和的氣候湊在一起的地方，村子就長成城鎮，城鎮再長成城市。
再看看空空的地方。沙漠太乾；高山和高原又冷、又陡、空氣又稀薄；寒帶的陽光永遠是斜的（第七課看過），地面還可能結凍。地球上標出來的幾個大沙漠，大約占陸地面積的 10%，卻只住了全世界大約 2% 的人，而且大多住在尼羅河這樣的河邊。海拔 3,000 公尺以上的地方大約占陸地的 3%，住了大約 0.5% 的人。
地勢低也很重要。1998 年的一項研究發現，世界上大約三分之一的人住在海拔不到 100 公尺的地方，但有人住的土地裡，這麼低的只占大約六分之一。用本頁的人口與高度資料算，答案幾乎一樣：大約 34% 的人住在大約 14% 的土地上。2016 年的一項研究估計，大約 40% 的人住在離海岸 100 公里以內。
為了比較不同的地方，地理學家用「人口密度」：人數除以土地面積。台灣是很擠的地方之一：民國 113 年（2024 年），台灣每平方公里大約有 646 人，臺北市超過 9,000 人。但即使在台灣，人也分布得不平均：大多數人住在平原和盆地，住在高山上的人很少。
questions: Why do so many people live along rivers, even rivers that flow through deserts?
Why do so few people live on high plateaus, in deserts, and in the polar zones?
Taiwan is crowded, but its high mountains are not. Why might that be?
answers: Rivers give water for drinking and for growing food, and the flat land beside them is easy to farm. Rivers also make travel and trade easier.
Deserts are too dry, high plateaus are cold with thin air, and the polar zones get only slanted sunlight and are often frozen. In all of them, it is hard to grow food.
The mountains are steep, high, and cooler, so it is hard to farm, build, and travel there. Most people live on the plains and in the basins.

myths.myth_en: People are spread out fairly evenly over the land.
myths.myth_zh: 人在陸地上分布得還算平均。
myths.fact_en: Not at all. Some river valleys and plains are packed, while huge deserts, mountains, and icy lands are nearly empty.
myths.fact_zh: 完全不是。有些河谷和平原擠滿了人，廣大的沙漠、高山和冰天雪地卻幾乎沒有人。

myths.myth_en: Most of the world's people live within 100 kilometers of the sea.
myths.myth_zh: 世界上大多數人住在離海 100 公里以內。
myths.fact_en: An estimate from 1990 said 60 percent, and it was repeated for years. A 2016 study, using more detailed data, found about 40 percent.
myths.fact_zh: 1990 年有一個估計說是 60%，這個數字被引用了很多年；2016 年一項用更細資料的研究，算出來大約是 40%。

myths.myth_en: Hot places near the equator have few people.
myths.myth_zh: 赤道附近很熱的地方，人很少。
myths.fact_en: Heat is not the problem; dryness is. Warm, wet places with good soil, such as the island of Java, are among the most crowded on Earth.
myths.fact_zh: 熱不是問題，乾才是。溫暖、潮濕、土壤又好的地方，像爪哇島，是地球上人最擠的地方之一。

myths.myth_en: High land always has few people.
myths.myth_zh: 地勢高的地方，人一定很少。
myths.fact_en: Not in the tropics. There, high land is cool instead of hot, and many people live on it. In the data on this page, tropical land above 2,000 meters covers about 1.1% of the land but holds about 2.4% of the people.
myths.fact_zh: 在熱帶不一定。熱帶的高地涼爽而不炎熱，住了很多人。用本頁的資料算，熱帶海拔 2,000 公尺以上的地方大約占陸地的 1.1%，卻住了大約 2.4% 的人。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Dots · 點背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Counting the people of the world

cards.body_en: The United Nations chose November 15, 2022, as the day the world's population was projected to reach 8 billion. It explained that people are living longer, thanks to better public health, nutrition, and medicine.
cards.body_zh: 聯合國把 2022 年 11 月 15 日訂為世界人口預計達到八十億的日子，並說明這是因為公共衛生、營養和醫療進步，人活得更久了。

cards.zh: 住在靠近海平面的地方
cards.body_en: Two scientists compared where people live with how high the land is. As of 1994, they estimated, 33.5 percent of the world's people lived less than 100 meters above sea level, while only 15.6 percent of inhabited land is that low. The middle person, they found, lived at 194 meters.
cards.body_zh: 兩位科學家把人住的地方和土地的高度對照。他們估計，到 1994 年，世界上 33.5% 的人住在海拔不到 100 公尺的地方，但有人住的土地裡只有 15.6% 這麼低。所有人依高度排成一列，正中間那個人住在 194 公尺。

cards.body_en: For years, people repeated a 1990 estimate that 60 percent of the world lived within 100 kilometers of a coast. A team in 2016 checked again with more detailed population and coastline data and found about 40 percent in 1990 and 39 percent in 2010. Good geography means checking the numbers.
cards.body_zh: 很多年來，大家一直引用 1990 年的估計：世界上 60% 的人住在離海岸 100 公里以內。2016 年一個研究團隊用更細的人口與海岸線資料重新算，1990 年大約是 40%，2010 年是 39%。好的地理學，就是要回頭檢查數字。

cards.body_en: According to the Executive Yuan, Taiwan had about 646 people per square kilometer in 2024. Taipei City, with 272 square kilometers, had 9,164 per square kilometer, the highest of any city or county. About 70 percent of Taiwan's people live in its six special municipalities.
cards.body_zh: 行政院的資料：民國 113 年，台灣每平方公里大約 646 人；臺北市面積 272 平方公里，每平方公里 9,164 人，是人口密度最高的都市。全國大約七成的人住在六個直轄市。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum (2018). In elementary school, population distribution first appears in grades 3–4. In junior high, it is taught for Taiwan and for regions of the world; the world as a whole comes back in senior high school.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要（民國 107 年發布）。人口分布在國小三、四年級第一次出現；國中先學臺灣、再學各區域；全世界的人口分布到高中再深入。

items.note_en: The game asks why people live where they do: water, land, and climate.
items.note_zh: 小遊戲問的就是人為什麼住在那裡：水、地形、氣候。

items.note_zh: 課綱裡這一條是在講東亞的一個區域；同樣的推理（水、農地、氣候）在哪裡都用得上。

sources.zh: 2022 年 11 月 15 日世界人口預計達到八十億
sources.src: United Nations, “Day of Eight Billion”

sources.en: “As of 1994, an estimated 1.88 × 10⁹ people, or 33.5% of the world's population, lived within 100 vertical meters of sea level, but only 15.6% of all inhabited land lies below 100 m elevation. The median person lived at an elevation of 194 m above sea level.”
sources.zh: 33.5% 的人住在海拔 100 公尺以內；中位數 194 公尺

sources.src: Kummu, M., and others (2016), “Over the hills and further away from coast: global geospatial patterns of human and environment over the 20th–21st centuries,” Environmental Research Letters 11(3)

sources.en: “Population density provides the number of people living on a given area of land (such as people per kilometer or per square mile).”

units.blurb_en: The island from above: its mountains and plains, its water, its people, its crops, its outer islands, and one county up close.
units.blurb_zh: 從天上看這座島：山與平原、水、人、作物、離島，再走近看一個縣。

lessons.title: What Does Taiwan Look Like from Above?
lessons.title_zh: 從天上看，台灣長什麼樣子？
lessons.blurb_en: Turn a 3D model of Taiwan made from real government elevation data, then cut it from west to east. See why the mountains sit east of the middle, the west is wide and gentle, and the east drops steeply to the sea.
lessons.blurb_zh: 轉動一座用政府真實高程資料做的立體台灣，再從西到東切一刀。看看為什麼高山偏在中間的東邊、西邊寬廣平緩、東邊陡陡地落進海裡。
lessons.big_idea_en: Taiwan's high mountains run from north to south, a little east of the middle. West of them, the land slopes gently down to wide plains, tablelands, and basins; east of them, it drops steeply to the sea. This shape decides where rivers flow and where people live.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 台灣的高山從北到南縱走，偏在中間的東邊。山的西邊緩緩地降到寬廣的平原、台地和盆地；東邊卻陡陡地落進海裡。這個形狀決定了河怎麼流、人住在哪裡。

lab.how_en: This is the real shape of Taiwan's main island, made from the Ministry of the Interior's elevation data. Drag to turn it, and tap anywhere to read the height. The red line is a cut from west to east: choose a place on the right or move the slider, and the drawing below shows the land along that line. Compare the west side of the mountains with the east side.
lab.how_zh: 這是臺灣本島真實的形狀，用內政部的高程資料做成。拖曳可以轉動，點任何地方可以讀出那裡的海拔。紅線是一條從西到東的切線：在右邊選一個地方或拖動滑桿，下面的圖就畫出沿著那條線的地形。比較山的西邊和東邊。

legend.en: Low green, higher yellow and brown, highest pale
legend.zh: 低處綠色，越高越黃褐，最高處淡色

lab.scale_en: Heights in the 3D model are exaggerated 5 times, and in the cut drawings 10 times; at true scale, even Taiwan's mountains would look almost flat. Each square is a 1-kilometer average, so the peaks come out lower than they really are: the highest square is about 3,695 meters, while Yushan's summit is 3,952 meters.
lab.scale_zh: 3D 模型的高度放大 5 倍，剖面圖放大 10 倍；照真實比例畫，連台灣的高山也幾乎是平的。每一格是 1 公里的平均，所以山頂會比實際矮：最高的一格大約 3,695 公尺，而玉山主峰是 3,952 公尺。
lab.credit_html: Height: the Ministry of the Interior's 2026 20-meter digital terrain model of Taiwan (main island), averaged by this page into 1-kilometer squares; a small area in the northern mountains with no data (about 140 square kilometers) was filled by averaging the squares around it. · 高程資料：內政部 2026年版全臺灣20公尺網格數值地形模型DTM資料 此開放資料依政府資料開放授權條款 (Open Government Data License) 進行公眾釋出，使用者於遵守本條款各項規定之前提下，得利用之。政府資料開放授權條款：https://data.gov.tw/license。本頁把它平均成 1 公里的格子；北部山區有一小塊原始資料沒有值（大約 140 平方公里），用四周的格子平均補起來。

cut.lead_en: Choose a line across Taiwan, or move it north and south. The drawing shows the land along the line, and the numbers compare the west side of the highest point with the east side.
cut.lead_zh: 選一條橫越台灣的線，或把它往南、往北移。圖上畫出沿線的地形，數字比較最高點的西邊和東邊。
cut.note_en: The slope is the average climb from the coast to the highest point on the line: meters of height for every kilometer you walk.
cut.note_zh: 坡度是從海岸到線上最高點的平均爬升：每往前走 1 公里，升高幾公尺。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four ways to look at Taiwan

parts.text_en: Look from the south: a long ridge of mountains runs the whole length of the island, closer to the east coast than to the west.
parts.text_zh: 從南邊看：一道長長的山脊貫穿全島，離東海岸比離西海岸近。

parts.text_en: Fly to Yushan and cut through it. The summit is 3,952 meters high, the highest in Taiwan.
parts.text_zh: 飛到玉山，從它切一刀。主峰高 3,952 公尺，是台灣最高的山。

parts.text_en: From the east, the mountains rise almost straight out of the sea. Through Changhua, the east side climbs about 105 meters for every kilometer.
parts.text_zh: 從東邊看，山幾乎從海裡直直升起。通過彰化的那條線，東邊每走 1 公里大約升高 105 公尺。

parts.text_en: From the west, the land rises slowly across plains and tablelands. On the same line, the west side climbs only about 33 meters per kilometer.
parts.text_zh: 從西邊看，地勢慢慢地升高，經過平原和台地。同一條線上，西邊每公里只升高大約 33 公尺。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Move the cut all the way north, then all the way south. Is the east side always the steeper one?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。把切線一路移到最北，再一路移到最南。東邊總是比較陡嗎？

form.en: What Kind of Land Is This?
form.lead_en: Eight places in Taiwan, each marked with a red dot. Read its height, the average height of the land around it, and the cut through it. Is it mountains, a tableland, a basin, a plain, or a longitudinal valley? You do not need to memorize any names; the numbers tell you. There is no timer.
form.lead_zh: 台灣的八個地方，各用一個紅點標出來。讀它的海拔、四周的平均海拔，和通過它的剖面。它是山地、台地、盆地、平原，還是縱谷？不用背地名，看數字就推得出來。不計時。
form.hint_en: Mountains: very high. Tableland: higher than all the land around it, with a flat top. Basin: low, with higher land on most sides. Plain: low and flat, open to the sea. Longitudinal valley: low, with high mountains on both the east and the west.
form.hint_zh: 山地：很高。台地：比四周都高，頂上平平的。盆地：低，大部分方向都比它高。平原：又低又平，朝海那邊敞開。縱谷：低，東西兩邊都是高山。
form.start_en: Compare here with the four directions around it.
form.start_zh: 拿「這裡」和四周四個方向比一比。
form.end_en: Now you can read a landform from numbers and a cross-section, anywhere on a map.
form.end_zh: 現在你可以在任何一張地圖上，從數字和剖面讀出地形。

questions.why_en: It is only a few meters above the sea, and the land to the north, west, and south is higher. A river leaves through the lower side.
questions.why_zh: 這裡只比海平面高幾公尺，北邊、西邊、南邊的地都比它高；河從比較低的那一邊流出去。

questions.why_en: Low and flat in every direction, and open to the sea on the west. This is Taiwan's largest plain.
questions.why_zh: 四面八方都又低又平，西邊朝海敞開。

questions.why_en: It stands a couple of hundred meters high, and the land in every direction around it is lower: a flat-topped table.
questions.why_zh: 它高出兩百多公尺，四周每個方向都比它低：一張頂上平平的「桌子」。

questions.why_en: A long, low strip with high mountains on both sides: the Central Mountain Range to the west and the Coastal Mountain Range to the east.
questions.why_zh: 一條長長的低地，兩邊都是高山：西邊是中央山脈，東邊是海岸山脈。

questions.why_en: More than 2,000 meters high. This is the backbone of the island.
questions.why_zh: 超過 2,000 公尺高，這是全島的主幹。

questions.why_en: Low land with tablelands to the west and hills to the east and north. Only the south side is lower.
questions.why_zh: 低地，西邊是台地，東邊和北邊是丘陵；只有南邊比較低。

questions.why_en: Low and flat, open to the sea on the east, with mountains behind it to the west and south.
questions.why_zh: 又低又平，東邊朝海敞開，西邊和南邊背後是山。

questions.why_en: A long, raised strip of land, higher than the plain to the west and the basin to the east. It runs right through Changhua.
questions.why_zh: 一條長長隆起的地，比西邊的平原、東邊的盆地都高；就在彰化。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for describing Taiwan's land
map_english.zh: 描述台灣地形的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about landforms. Listen, repeat, then describe the land where you live to a friend from another country.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說地形。先聽、再跟著唸，然後向一位外國朋友描述你住的地方的地形。

items.en: Taiwan's mountains run from north to south.
items.zh: 台灣的山從北到南縱走。

items.en: The highest mountain in Taiwan is Yushan.
items.zh: 台灣最高的山是玉山。

items.en: Yushan is about 3,952 meters high.
items.zh: 玉山大約 3,952 公尺高。

items.en: The west coast is flat and low.
items.zh: 西海岸又平又低。

items.en: On the east coast, the mountains drop steeply into the sea.
items.zh: 在東海岸，山陡陡地落進海裡。

items.en: Taipei lies in a basin.
items.zh: 臺北位在一個盆地裡。

items.en: The Huadong Valley lies between two mountain ranges.
items.zh: 花東縱谷位在兩條山脈之間。

items.en: What is the land like where you live?
items.zh: 你住的地方，地形是什麼樣子？

tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住台灣的形狀

tricks.title_en: High in the middle, a little east
tricks.body_en: The main ridge runs north to south, closer to the east coast.
tricks.body_zh: 主要的山脊南北縱走，離東海岸比較近。

tricks.body_en: The west slopes down slowly; the east drops fast.
tricks.body_zh: 西邊慢慢降下來，東邊一下子就落下去。

tricks.body_en: Low in the middle, higher land around it.
tricks.body_zh: 中間低，四周高。

tricks.body_en: A flat top, higher than the land around it.
tricks.body_zh: 頂上平平的，比四周高。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Use a plastic knife or a piece of string to cut the clay model, never a sharp blade.
safety.zh: 切黏土模型用塑膠刀或一條線，不要用尖銳的刀片。

safety.en: Keep clay away from your mouth, and wash your hands when you finish.
safety.zh: 黏土不要放進嘴裡，做完要洗手。

safety.en: Cover the desk with newspaper or a mat before you start.
safety.zh: 開始之前先在桌上鋪報紙或墊子。

safety.en: When you look at real mountains, stay on marked trails and with an adult; mountain weather can change quickly.
safety.zh: 去看真的山時，要走在步道上、有大人陪同；山上的天氣變化很快。

materials.en: A printed outline of Taiwan, about 30 centimeters long
materials.zh: 一張大約 30 公分長的台灣輪廓圖

materials.en: Modeling clay in two or three colors
A piece of string or dental floss
A ruler

steps.en: Look at the 3D model from the south. Notice where the mountains are highest.
steps.zh: 從南邊看 3D 模型，注意山最高的地方在哪裡。

steps.en: Press a thin layer of clay over the whole outline for the plains.
steps.zh: 在整張輪廓上壓一層薄薄的黏土，當作平原。

steps.en: Add a long ridge of clay for the mountains. Put it closer to the east coast, and make the east side steeper.
steps.zh: 加上一長條黏土當作高山，放在比較靠東海岸的地方，東邊做得比較陡。

steps.en: Cut the model from west to east with the string, near Changhua. Look at the cut face from the side.
steps.zh: 在靠近彰化的地方，用線從西到東把模型切開，從側面看切開的那一面。

steps.en: Compare your cut with the cut on this page. What did you get right, and what would you change?
steps.zh: 拿你的切面和本頁的剖面比一比。哪裡做對了？哪裡要改？

activities.tip_en: Your model is probably taller than the real Taiwan would be at this size. That is vertical exaggeration, and the 3D model on this page does it too.
activities.tip_zh: 照這個大小，你的模型多半比真的台灣高很多。這叫做「垂直誇大」，本頁的 3D 模型也這樣做。

materials.en: Graph paper
A pencil and a ruler
The “Cut the Island” activity on this page

steps.en: Choose one line in “Cut the Island.” Write down the highest point and how far it is from each coast.
steps.zh: 在「切一刀」選一條線，寫下最高點的高度，以及它離兩邊海岸各多遠。

steps.en: On graph paper, let one square across be 10 kilometers. Mark the two coasts and the highest point.
steps.zh: 在方格紙上，橫的一格代表 10 公里，標出兩邊的海岸和最高點。

steps.en: Choose a height scale, for example one square up for every 500 meters. Draw the mountain between the coasts.
steps.zh: 選一個高度的比例，例如往上一格代表 500 公尺，在兩個海岸之間畫出這座山。

steps.en: Work out how many times you exaggerated the height. (Hint: compare 10 kilometers across with 500 meters up.)
steps.zh: 算一算你把高度放大了幾倍。（提示：拿橫的 10 公里和直的 500 公尺比。）

steps.en: Which side of your drawing is steeper? Does it match the page?
steps.zh: 你畫的圖哪一邊比較陡？和本頁一樣嗎？

activities.tip_en: If one square across is 10 kilometers and one square up is 500 meters, the heights are exaggerated 20 times.
activities.tip_zh: 如果橫的一格是 10 公里、直的一格是 500 公尺，高度就放大了 20 倍。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, numbers, and quotations on this page were checked against these sources (November 2026). The 3D model, the cuts, the slopes, and the answers to the game are computed by the page itself from the elevation data and tested automatically
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代、數字與引文依下列資料查證（2026 年 11 月）；3D 模型、剖面、坡度和小遊戲的答案，都由頁面用高程資料自己計算，並有自動測試
paras: From an airplane or a satellite, Taiwan's main island looks like a long spindle, wide in the middle and narrow at both ends. According to the Executive Yuan, it is 394 kilometers from north to south and 144 kilometers across at its widest. The Tropic of Cancer, from Lesson 7, crosses it near Chiayi.

Most of the island is mountains. The Executive Yuan lists five ranges, from east to west: the Coastal Mountain Range, the Central Mountain Range, the Xueshan Range, the Yushan Range, and the Alishan Range. In the elevation data used on this page, about 31 out of every 100 squares of land are higher than 1,000 meters, and only about 29 out of 100 are lower than 100 meters.

The highest peak is Yushan. In 2022, surveyors from the National Land Surveying and Mapping Center carried their instruments up the trail and measured its main peak at 3,952.433 meters, give or take 0.046 meters. The government's Taiwan portal counts 268 peaks higher than 3,000 meters.

The mountains are not in the exact middle. Cut the island from west to east through Changhua: the highest point on that line, about 3,163 meters, is 96 kilometers from the west coast but only 30 kilometers from the east coast. So the east side is about three times as steep as the west side. On the east coast, the mountains drop almost straight into the sea.

West of the Alishan Range, the land becomes gentler. From north to south, the Executive Yuan lists the Taipei Basin, the tablelands of Taoyuan, Hsinchu, and Miaoli, the Taichung Basin, the Chianan Plain, and the Pingtung Plain. In the east there is much less flat land: the narrow Huadong Longitudinal Valley lies between the Central and Coastal Mountain Ranges, and the Lanyang Plain opens to the sea in the northeast.

This shape matters. The Central Mountain Range is the divide between the rivers that flow east and those that flow west. Because the west side is wider, its rivers are longer: the Zhuoshui River, Taiwan's longest at 186.6 kilometers, starts high in the mountains and reaches the sea between Changhua and Yunlin. And most of Taiwan's people live on the wide, gentle west side, as Lesson 8 would predict.
paras_zh: 從飛機或衛星上看，臺灣本島像一個長長的紡錘，中間寬、兩頭窄。行政院的資料說，它南北長 394 公里，東西最寬的地方 144 公里。第七課的北回歸線，就在嘉義附近穿過它。
島上大部分是山。行政院列出五條山脈，由東到西是：海岸山脈、中央山脈、雪山山脈、玉山山脈和阿里山山脈。在本頁用的高程資料裡，陸地每 100 格大約有 31 格高於 1,000 公尺，低於 100 公尺的只有大約 29 格。
最高峰是玉山。民國 111 年（2022 年），國土測繪中心的測量人員把儀器沿著步道一路背上山，量得玉山主峰高 3,952.433 公尺，誤差在 0.046 公尺之內。政府的台灣入口網說，台灣有 268 座超過 3,000 公尺的山峰。
山不在正中間。從彰化從西到東切一刀：那條線上的最高點大約 3,163 公尺，離西海岸 96 公里，離東海岸卻只有 30 公里。所以東邊大約比西邊陡三倍。在東海岸，山幾乎是直直地落進海裡。
阿里山山脈以西，地勢變得平緩。行政院由北到南列出：臺北盆地、桃竹苗臺地、臺中盆地、嘉南平原和屏東平原。東部的平地少得多：窄窄的花東縱谷夾在中央山脈和海岸山脈之間，蘭陽平原則在東北朝海敞開。
這個形狀很重要。中央山脈是東、西部河川的分水嶺。西邊比較寬，河就比較長：台灣最長的濁水溪，主流長 186.6 公里，從高山一路流到彰化和雲林之間入海。而台灣大多數的人住在寬廣平緩的西部——正如第八課會預測的。
questions: Why are the rivers on Taiwan's west side longer than those on the east side?
Why does a 3D model of Taiwan need vertical exaggeration?
Where do you think most of Taiwan's farms and cities are, and why?
answers: The main ridge is closer to the east coast, so there is more land between the mountains and the sea on the west. The rivers have farther to go.
Taiwan is hundreds of kilometers long but only about 4 kilometers high. At true scale, the mountains would look almost flat.
On the plains and in the basins of the west, where the land is low and flat, and rivers bring water.

myths.myth_en: Taiwan's mountains are right in the middle of the island.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣的山就在島的正中間。
myths.fact_en: They are east of the middle. Through Changhua, the highest point is 96 kilometers from the west coast but only 30 kilometers from the east coast.
myths.fact_zh: 偏在中間的東邊。通過彰化的那條線，最高點離西海岸 96 公里，離東海岸只有 30 公里。

myths.myth_en: A 3D model shows how steep the mountains really are.
myths.myth_zh: 立體模型呈現的就是山真正的陡度。
myths.fact_en: Most 3D models of Taiwan stretch the heights. This page's model makes them 5 times taller, and its cross-sections 10 times, or the mountains would look almost flat.
myths.fact_zh: 大多數台灣的立體模型都把高度拉高。本頁的模型放大 5 倍、剖面放大 10 倍，不然山看起來幾乎是平的。

myths.myth_en: A basin is closed in on every side.
myths.myth_zh: 盆地四面八方都被圍住。
myths.fact_en: Most basins have a lower side where a river flows out. In the data, the Taichung Basin is lower to the south than it is to the east, west, and north.
myths.fact_zh: 大多數盆地有一邊比較低，河從那裡流出去。在資料裡，臺中盆地的南邊比東、西、北三邊都低。

myths.myth_en: The east of Taiwan is nothing but mountains.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣的東部全都是山。
myths.fact_en: There is less flat land in the east, but not none: the Huadong Longitudinal Valley and the Lanyang Plain are home to towns and farms.
myths.fact_zh: 東部的平地比較少，但不是沒有：花東縱谷和蘭陽平原上都有城鎮和農田。

cards.en: Carrying a level up the mountain
cards.body_en: In October 2022, surveyors from the National Land Surveying and Mapping Center measured Yushan step by step, from a benchmark at Tataka up the trail to the main peak, using 23 survey points. Their result: 3,952.433 meters, give or take 0.046 meters.
cards.body_zh: 2022 年 10 月，國土測繪中心的測量人員從塔塔加的一等水準點出發，沿著登山步道選了 23 個點，一段一段量到玉山主峰。結果是 3,952.433 公尺，誤差在 0.046 公尺之內。

cards.body_en: The Executive Yuan describes the main island as spindle-shaped, 394 kilometers from north to south and 144 kilometers across at its widest, with a coastline of 1,150.95 kilometers.
cards.body_zh: 行政院說，臺灣本島呈紡錘形，南北縱長 394 公里，東西最大寬度 144 公里，環島海岸線長 1,150.95 公里。

cards.body_en: The Zhuoshui River starts between the main and east peaks of Hehuan Mountain, at 3,220 meters, and runs 186.6 kilometers to the sea between Dacheng in Changhua and Mailiao in Yunlin.
cards.body_zh: 濁水溪發源於合歡山主峰與東峰之間（海拔 3,220 公尺），主流長 186.6 公里，在彰化縣大城鄉與雲林縣麥寮鄉之間入海。

cards.zh: 用 20 公尺方格拼成的地圖
cards.body_en: The Ministry of the Interior shares a height for every 20-meter square of Taiwan as open data. This page averages them into 1-kilometer squares: 36,417 squares of land. In that 20-meter data, the highest point near Yushan is 3,947.46 meters, a few meters below the surveyed summit, because each square is an average.
cards.body_zh: 內政部把臺灣每一個 20 公尺方格的高度，當作開放資料公開。本頁把它們平均成 1 公里的格子：陸地共 36,417 格。在 20 公尺的資料裡，玉山附近最高的一格是 3,947.46 公尺，比實測的主峰矮幾公尺，因為每一格都是平均。

lessons.title: Why Can Taiwan Run Short of Water When It Rains So Much?
lessons.title_zh: 台灣雨這麼多，為什麼還會缺水？
lessons.blurb_en: Let it rain on a 3D model of Taiwan and follow the raindrops to the sea. See why short, steep rivers and a rainy season only half a year long can leave a rainy island short of water.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在立體的台灣上下一場雨，跟著雨滴一路流到海。看看為什麼又短又陡的河、只有半年的雨季，會讓一座多雨的島也缺水。
lessons.big_idea_en: Taiwan gets a lot of rain, but most of it falls in a few months, and its short, steep rivers carry it quickly to the sea. Many people share the water that is left. So even a rainy island has to store water in reservoirs and save it.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 台灣的雨很多，但大多下在幾個月裡，又短又陡的河很快就把雨水送進海裡；剩下的水還要分給很多人。所以即使是多雨的島，也得用水庫把水存起來、省著用。

lab.title_en: Follow the Rain to the Sea
lab.how_en: Rain is falling on Taiwan. Each light blue drop runs downhill along the rivers, which the page works out from the shape of the land, until it reaches the sea. Tap anywhere on the land to drop one raindrop there: its path turns gold, and the panel tells you how far it travels, how high it starts, and where it reaches the sea. Try the west side of the mountains, then the east.
lab.how_zh: 台灣正在下雨。每一顆淡藍色的雨滴都順著河往下流（河是頁面從地形算出來的），一直流到海。點地形上任何一個地方，就在那裡下一滴雨：它的路會變成金色，右邊告訴你它走了多遠、從多高的地方出發、從哪裡入海。先試試山的西邊，再試試東邊。

legend.en: Raindrops on their way to the sea
Rivers worked out from the land
The path of the drop you chose

lab.scale_en: Heights are exaggerated 5 times. The rivers come from the 1-kilometer land model: water always moves to the lowest neighboring square, so the rivers are straighter and a little shorter than real ones, and small streams are not drawn. The drops move at the same speed everywhere, only to show the paths; they do not show how fast real water flows.
lab.scale_zh: 高度放大 5 倍。河是從 1 公里的地形算出來的：水一律流向四周最低的那一格，所以畫出來的河比真的直、也短一點，小溪沒有畫。雨滴在哪裡都走一樣快，只是為了讓你看見路線，不代表真的水流多快。
lab.note_en: Rain on the west side usually has a long way to go; rain on the east side reaches the sea quickly.
lab.note_zh: 落在西邊的雨，通常要走很遠；落在東邊的雨，很快就到海了。
